# Marks & anatomy
The quiet, considered look is a few fixed specs plus two pieces of negative space.
The data is the only thing allowed to be loud.
## Mark specs (fixed across every chart)
| Mark | Spec |
|---|---|
| Bar / column | **<= 24px thick** (cap it - never fill the slot; let the band's leftover be air); **4px rounded data-end, square at the baseline**; grows from a single baseline |
| Line | **2px**, round join/cap |
| Marker / end-dot | **>= 8px** (r >= 4), filled with the series color |
| Area fill | the series hue at **~10% opacity** (a wash, never a saturated block) |
| Gridlines / axes | one-step-off-surface gray, **hairline (1px), solid** (never dashed), recessive |
## The two spacers (white doing the separating)
- **Surface gap.** A **2px gap** in the surface color separates touching marks - every
  segment of a stacked bar, and every adjacent (touching) bar, the same width. Keep it
  one consistent width across a stack; neighbors one step apart read distinct because of
  the gap, not a stroke drawn around them.
- **Surface ring.** Dots and end-markers carry a **2px ring in the surface color**,
  so they stay legible where they cross a line or overlap each other. The ring is part
  of the mark's hover/hit target, not just spacing - see `interaction.md` (small dots
  are easy to under-size for hover).
Never draw a border around a mark to separate it. The gap and the ring are the
mechanism; a stroke adds data-weight ink that isn't data.
## Labels & legend
A **legend is always present for two or more series** - the dependable identity
channel; never make the reader rely on color-matching alone. Direct labels then ride
the marks to *supplement* it. **A single series needs no legend box**: there is only
one color, so the chart's title or subtitle already says what is plotted. A box with
one swatch restates the title and costs space.
- **Label selectively - never a number on every point.** A value beside every dot or
  segment is chaos and goes unread. Label the endpoint, the extreme, or the one series
  the story is about; let the axis, the legend, and the tooltip/table carry the rest.
  Direct labels work *because* they are sparing - flood the chart and they stop working.
- **Direct labels before gridlines; gridlines before a second axis.**
- **A label that won't fit doesn't get clipped - measure first.** Only place a label
  *inside* a bar or stacked segment when the rendered text fits with comfortable
  padding on both sides. If it doesn't fit: for a whole bar/column, move the label
  outside the bar end (or to the tooltip if there's no room outside either); for an
  *interior* stacked segment (which has no free end),
  skip the inline label and let the legend + tooltip carry it. Either way the value
  stays in the table view, so nothing is gated. Never use `overflow: hidden` on the
  segment to "solve" it - that crops the first/last characters and is worse than no
  label. Text never overflows or is clipped by its own mark.
- Bars -> value at the tip. Columns -> value on the cap. Lines -> value at the end.
- Y-axis ticks: round to clean numbers, compact from 1,000 up (0 / 1K / 2K); they
  carry the values you didn't directly label, so keep them unless every value is labeled.
- **Text never wears the data color.** Marks - bars, lines, dots, area fills - carry
  the series color; labels, values, legends, and axis text use **text tokens**
  (primary / secondary / muted). A light categorical hue (yellow, aqua) is illegible
  as text on the surface. Identity comes from the colored mark *beside* the text - a
  dot, a short line-key, a swatch - never from coloring the text itself. A label set
  *inside* a colored fill (a stacked segment, a map tile) is the one exception: white or
  near-black, the same two in both modes, by the fill's luminance. `palette.md` says which its
  categorical and status colors take.
- **When end-labels collide, don't stack them.** Direct end-labels work when series
  separate at the right edge. When lines converge, nudging labels apart vertically
  detaches them from their lines and reads as noise - instead use **leader lines**
  (a thin connector from label to line-end), facet into **small multiples**, or fall
  back to the legend + tooltip. Past ~4 converging series, small multiples is usually right.
## Figures - when the form is a number
- **Stat tile** contract: `label` (sentence case, no trailing colon) · `value` (Sans
  semibold, auto-compact: 1,284 / 12.9K / $4.2M) · `delta` (optional; signed,
  vs a named period; color = direction × whether up is good) · `trend` (optional;
  12-point sparkline in the de-emphasis hue, current period in the accent).
- **Meter:** the fill carries severity (accent -> warning -> danger); the unfilled
  track is a **lighter step of the same ramp** (blue-on-blue, etc.) so state reads
  across the whole bar.
- **Hero figure.** The single number a dashboard leads with, >=48px, in the same
  sans as everything else (never a display or serif face - it reads as off-brand
  decoration). Exactly one per view.
- **Proportional figures for big numbers; tabular only in columns.** A large
  standalone value (hero figure, stat-tile value) uses the font's default
  proportional figures - `tabular-nums` gives every digit the width of a `0`, so a
  number like `121` looks loose at display sizes. Reserve
  `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns of numbers that must align
  vertically (table rows, axis ticks).

"""Reprint clusters, for eval A's reprint signal: a syndicated story was printed in many
papers in the same words, give or take OCR errors, so articles that share a run of words are
taken for printings of one story."""

import re
import zlib

WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z]{3,}")
RUN, OPENING, ONE_IN = 7, 120, 8  # words per run, words read, one run kept in ONE_IN
BOILERPLATE = 1000  # a run more articles than this share is stock phrasing, not a story
DOC_BITS = 21  # room for 2 million documents beside each key


def keys(text):
    """64-bit hashes of a sample of the seven-word runs in the article's opening. A run is
    kept by its own hash, so the sample doesn't shift when one printing has an extra line."""
    words = WORD.findall((text or "")[:6000].replace("-\n", "").lower())[:OPENING]
    found = set()
    for i in range(len(words) - RUN + 1):
        run = " ".join(words[i : i + RUN]).encode()
        low = zlib.crc32(run)
        if low % ONE_IN == 0:  # a second, differently seeded CRC keeps chance collisions out
            found.add(zlib.crc32(run, 0x5BD1E995) << 32 | low)
    return found


def clusters(doc_keys, boilerplate=BOILERPLATE):
    """The groups of two or more documents linked by shared keys, as sorted lists of their
    indexes. Keys are sorted with their documents packed beside them, which takes far less
    memory than a dictionary of lists for a million articles."""
    assert len(doc_keys) < 1 << DOC_BITS
    parent = list(range(len(doc_keys)))

    def root(doc):
        while parent[doc] != doc:
            parent[doc] = parent[parent[doc]]
            doc = parent[doc]
        return doc

    mask = (1 << DOC_BITS) - 1
    entries = sorted(key << DOC_BITS | doc for doc, held in enumerate(doc_keys) for key in held)
    start = 0
    for end in range(1, len(entries) + 1):
        if end < len(entries) and entries[end] >> DOC_BITS == entries[start] >> DOC_BITS:
            continue
        if 2 <= end - start <= boilerplate:
            first = root(entries[start] & mask)
            for entry in entries[start + 1 : end]:
                other = root(entry & mask)
                if other != first:
                    parent[other] = first
        start = end
    groups = {}
    for doc in range(len(doc_keys)):
        groups.setdefault(root(doc), []).append(doc)
    return [group for group in groups.values() if len(group) > 1]

"""make eval: eval A over the archive read in Phase 2A. It writes eval/results/eval_a.json,
and its charts and hand-judged samples to eval/results/eval_a/.

1. EDA: by year, by state and by term; candidate lengths; OCR quality, as the share of words
   /usr/share/dict/words knows; and reprint clusters among the candidates.
2. Composition: 200 candidates at random, each put in a category by hand in
   composition.json.
3. Recall: 300 articles from the near-miss reservoirs and 300 from the random ones, each
   weighted by its year's share of the pool, marked by hand in recall.json.

Every sample is seeded, so a rerun draws the same articles and keeps the judgments made.
"""

import json
import random
import re
import zlib
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import zstandard

from paperghosts.cluster.reprints import clusters, keys
from paperghosts.ingest import lexicon
from paperghosts.ingest.prefilter import SAMPLE_SIZE
from paperghosts.ingest.year import code_version
from paperghosts.stats import wilson

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DATA = ROOT / "data"
RESULTS = ROOT / "eval" / "results"
OUT = RESULTS / "eval_a"
DICTIONARY = Path("/usr/share/dict/words")
OCR_ONE_IN = 20  # OCR quality is measured on one candidate in twenty, chosen by its id
COMPOSITION, RECALL, REPRINT_CHECK = 200, 300, 20
CATEGORIES = (
    "ghost_report",
    "fiction",
    "religious",
    "figurative",
    "name_or_title",
    "social_event",
    "other",
)
WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z]{3,}")
# common endings, tried in turn when a word isn't in the list as it stands
ENDINGS = (
    ("ies", "y"),
    ("ied", "y"),
    ("ing", "e"),
    ("ing", ""),
    ("ed", "e"),
    ("ed", ""),
    ("es", ""),
    ("s", ""),
    ("ly", ""),
)
# words to look around in a random-pool article, besides its opening; a guide to reading
FLAGS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:spirit|spectral|unearthly|uncanny|weird|supernatural|seance|apparit|phantasm"
    r"|spook|wraith|goblin|banshee|witch|hoodoo|voodoo|superstiti|haint|bogey|boogey"
    r"|corpse|graveyard|midnight|in white|strange (?:noise|light|sound)|mysterious|knock"
    r"|rapp|haunt|spectre|specter|phantom|[gq][hbk]?[o0ae][a-z]?sts?\b)\w*",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_words = None


def dictionary():
    global _words
    if _words is None:
        _words = frozenset(w.strip().lower() for w in DICTIONARY.read_text().splitlines())
    return _words


def known(word, words):
    if word in words:
        return True
    return any(
        len(word) > len(end) + 2 and word.endswith(end) and word[: -len(end)] + back in words
        for end, back in ENDINGS
    )


def ocr_quality(text, words, least=20):
    """The share of the article's words of three letters or more that the dictionary knows,
    once line-break hyphens are joined and common endings come off; None under `least`."""
    found = WORD.findall((text or "").replace("-\n", "").lower())
    if len(found) < least:
        return None
    return sum(known(word, words) for word in found) / len(found)


def draw(pools, sizes, n, seed):
    """n (year, item) pairs, each year drawn in proportion to its share of the pool across the
    archive, so the sample stands for every article in the pool rather than for each year
    equally. pools maps a year to its reservoir, and sizes to the pool's full size."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    years = sorted(year for year in pools if sizes.get(year) and pools[year])
    wanted = Counter(rng.choices(years, weights=[sizes[year] for year in years], k=n))
    return [
        (year, item)
        for year in years
        for item in rng.sample(list(pools[year]), min(wanted[year], len(pools[year])))
    ]


def uniform(counts, n, seed):
    """n (year, index) pairs without replacement, every candidate equally likely."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    years = sorted(counts)
    picks = []
    for left in sorted(rng.sample(range(sum(counts.values())), n)):
        for year in years:
            if left < counts[year]:
                picks.append((year, left))
                break
            left -= counts[year]
    return picks


def window(text, position, width=320):
    start = max(0, position - width // 2)
    return " ".join(text[start : start + width].split())


def first_match(text, forms):
    low = text.lower()
    found = [low.find(form.lower()) for form in forms]
    return min([p for p in found if p >= 0], default=0)


def year_pass(job):
    """One year's candidates: per-article length, OCR quality for a fixed sample, reprint keys,
    paper and opening; plus the composition picks and recall picks that fall in this year."""
    year, wanted, near, rand = job
    words, docs, picked = dictionary(), [], []
    with zstandard.open(DATA / "candidates" / f"{year}.jsonl.zst", "rt") as rows:
        for index, row in enumerate(map(json.loads, rows)):
            text = row["text"] or ""
            quality = None
            if zlib.crc32(row["article_id"].encode()) % OCR_ONE_IN == 0:
                quality = ocr_quality(text, words)
            docs.append(
                (
                    len(text.split()),
                    quality,
                    tuple(keys(text)),
                    row["lccn"],
                    row["article_id"],
                    f"{row['paper'] or '?'} {row['date']}: {' '.join(text[:200].split())}",
                )
            )
            if index in wanted:
                both = f"{row['headline'] or ''}\n{text}"
                forms = [form for found in row["terms"].values() for form in found]
                picked.append(
                    {
                        "article_id": row["article_id"],
                        "year": year,
                        "date": row["date"],
                        "paper": row["paper"],
                        "state": row["state"],
                        "terms": sorted(row["terms"]),
                        "words": len(text.split()),
                        "headline": " / ".join((row["headline"] or "").split("\n"))[:200],
                        "context": window(both, first_match(both, forms), 600),
                        "category": None,
                        "note": None,
                    }
                )
    recalled = []
    if near or rand:
        seen = Counter()
        with zstandard.open(DATA / "samples" / f"{year}.jsonl.zst", "rt") as rows:
            for row in map(json.loads, rows):
                pool, index = row["sample"], seen[row["sample"]]
                seen[pool] += 1
                if index not in (near if pool == "near_miss" else rand):
                    continue
                text = row["text"] or ""
                low = text.lower()
                spots = [m.start() for m in FLAGS.finditer(text)]
                spots += [low.find(t) for t in row["near_miss_terms"] for t in (t[:5],)]
                recalled.append(
                    {
                        "pool": pool,
                        "article_id": row["article_id"],
                        "year": year,
                        "date": row["date"],
                        "paper": row["paper"],
                        "headline": " / ".join((row["headline"] or "").split("\n"))[:200],
                        "near_miss_terms": sorted(row["near_miss_terms"]),
                        "words": len(text.split()),
                        "opening": " ".join(text[:420].split()),
                        "contexts": [window(text, p, 300) for p in sorted(set(spots))[:4] if p >= 0],
                        "ghost_report": None,
                        "note": None,
                    }
                )
    return year, docs, picked, recalled


def quantiles(values, points=(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.99)):
    ordered = sorted(values)
    return {f"p{round(q * 100)}": ordered[round(q * (len(ordered) - 1))] for q in points}


def keep_judgments(path, items, key, fields):
    """The freshly drawn items, with any judgment already made on them carried over."""
    if path.exists():
        made = {key(old): old for old in json.loads(path.read_text())}
        for item in items:
            for field in fields:
                item[field] = made.get(key(item), {}).get(field)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(items, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return items


def rate(hits, n, of):
    low, high = wilson(hits, n)
    return {
        "count": hits,
        "n": n,
        "share": hits / n,
        "low": low,
        "high": high,
        "implied": round(hits / n * of),
        "implied_low": round(low * of),
        "implied_high": round(high * of),
    }


def main():
    from charts import draw_all  # noqa: PLC0415 (the charts are only needed here)

    counts = {
        c["year"]: c for c in (json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in (DATA / "counts").glob("*.json"))
    }
    years = sorted(counts)
    total = {k: sum(counts[y][k] for y in years) for k in ("pages", "articles", "candidates", "near_miss")}
    others = {y: counts[y]["articles"] - counts[y]["candidates"] for y in years}
    total["non_candidates"] = sum(others.values())

    composition = defaultdict(set)
    for year, index in uniform({y: counts[y]["candidates"] for y in years}, COMPOSITION, "eval A composition"):

    near, rand = defaultdict(set), defaultdict(set)
    reservoirs = {y: range(min(SAMPLE_SIZE, counts[y]["near_miss"])) for y in years}
    for year, index in draw(reservoirs, {y: counts[y]["near_miss"] for y in years}, RECALL, "eval A recall near-miss"):
        near[year].add(index)
    reservoirs = {y: range(min(SAMPLE_SIZE, others[y])) for y in years}
    for year, index in draw(reservoirs, others, RECALL, "eval A recall random"):
        rand[year].add(index)

    docs, years_of, picked, recalled = [], [], [], []
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool:
        for year, found, chosen, reread in pool.map(year_pass, sorted(jobs, key=lambda job: -counts[job[0]]["articles"])):

            years_of += [year] * len(found)
            picked += chosen

    lengths = [doc[0] for doc in docs]

    groups = clusters([doc[2] for doc in docs])
    group_sizes = sorted((len(g) for g in groups), reverse=True)
    cross = [g for g in groups if len({docs[d][3] for d in g}) > 1]

    checks = []
    for group in rng.sample(groups, min(REPRINT_CHECK, len(groups))):
        a, b = rng.sample(group, 2)
        checks.append(

                "openings": [docs[a][5], docs[b][5]],

    largest = [

    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    picked = keep_judgments(OUT / "composition.json", sorted(picked, key=lambda p: (p["year"], p["article_id"])), lambda p: p["article_id"], ("category", "note"))
    recalled = keep_judgments(OUT / "recall.json", sorted(recalled, key=lambda r: (r["pool"], r["year"], r["article_id"])), lambda r: (r["pool"], r["article_id"]), ("ghost_report", "note"))
    checks = keep_judgments(OUT / "reprint-check.json", checks, lambda c: tuple(c["members"]), ("same_story",))

    by_state = defaultdict(Counter)

    report = {

        "lexicon_version": lexicon.VERSION,
        "code_version": code_version(),
        "totals": {**total, "candidates_per_million": total["candidates"] / total["articles"] * 1e6},
        "by_year": [

            "share_of_articles": by_state["unknown"]["articles"] / total["articles"],

            "cross_paper_clusters": len(cross),

LENGTH_BINS = (0, 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200)
SIZE_BINS = ((2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 4), (5, 9), (10, 19), (20, 49), (50, 10**9))


def length_histogram(lengths):
    edges = list(LENGTH_BINS) + [10**9]
    return [
        {"from": lo, "to": hi - 1 if hi < 10**9 else None, "candidates": sum(1 for n in lengths if lo <= n < hi)}
        for lo, hi in zip(edges, edges[1:], strict=False)
    ]


def size_histogram(sizes):
    return [
        {"from": lo, "to": hi if hi < 10**9 else None, "clusters": sum(1 for s in sizes if lo <= s <= hi), "candidates": sum(s for s in sizes if lo <= s <= hi)}
        for lo, hi in SIZE_BINS
    ]


def summarise_checks(checks):
    judged = [c for c in checks if c["same_story"] is not None]
    same = sum(bool(c["same_story"]) for c in judged)
    return {"judged": len(judged), "same_story": same, **({"low": wilson(same, len(judged))[0], "high": wilson(same, len(judged))[1]} if judged else {})}


def summarise_composition(picked, candidates):
    judged = [p for p in picked if p["category"]]
    out = {"sample": len(picked), "judged": len(judged), "seed": "eval A composition"}
    if judged:
        out["categories"] = {c: rate(sum(p["category"] == c for p in judged), len(judged), candidates) for c in CATEGORIES}
    return out


def summarise_recall(recalled, total):
    out = {}
    for pool, size, seed in (("near_miss", total["near_miss"], "eval A recall near-miss"), ("random", total["non_candidates"], "eval A recall random")):
        items = [r for r in recalled if r["pool"] == pool]
        judged = [r for r in items if r["ghost_report"] is not None]
        found = [r for r in judged if r["ghost_report"]]
        out[pool] = {"sample": len(items), "judged": len(judged), "seed": seed, "pool_size": size}
        if judged:
            out[pool].update(rate(len(found), len(judged), size))
            out[pool]["reports"] = [{k: r[k] for k in ("article_id", "year", "date", "paper", "headline", "note")} for r in found]
    return out

    yield f"reprints: {r['clusters']:,} clusters hold {r['clustered_candidates']:,} candidates ({r['share_clustered']:.1%}); {r['distinct_stories']:,} distinct stories; {r['cross_paper_clusters']:,} clusters span papers"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Eval A's charts, as standalone SVG files with a light and a dark theme and a tooltip on
every mark. They follow the dataviz rules: one axis, thin marks with rounded data ends,
recessive grid lines, and text in ink colors, never in a series color."""

from html import escape

STYLE = """<style>
.bg{fill:#fcfcfb}.ink{fill:#0b0b0b}.muted{fill:#52514e}.grid{stroke:#e6e5e1;stroke-width:1}
.axis{stroke:#c3c2b7;stroke-width:1}.s1{fill:#2a78d6}.s2{fill:#eb6834}.wash{fill:#2a78d6;fill-opacity:.1}
.line{fill:none;stroke:#2a78d6;stroke-width:2;stroke-linejoin:round;stroke-linecap:round}
.whisker{stroke:#0b0b0b;stroke-width:1.5}.hit{fill:transparent}
text{font-family:-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px}
.title{font-size:15px;font-weight:600}
@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){
.bg{fill:#1a1a19}.ink{fill:#f0efec}.muted{fill:#c3c2b7}.grid{stroke:#333331}.axis{stroke:#52514e}
.s1{fill:#3987e5}.s2{fill:#d95926}.wash{fill:#3987e5}.line{stroke:#3987e5}.whisker{stroke:#f0efec}}
</style>"""
WIDTH = 760


def compact(value):
    for size, suffix in ((1e9, "B"), (1e6, "M"), (1e3, "K")):
        if abs(value) >= size:
            return f"{value / size:.1f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".") + suffix
    return f"{value:g}"


def nice(top, ticks=4):
    """A round upper bound and step for an axis that reaches `top`."""
    raw = max(top, 1e-9) / ticks
    power = 10 ** len(str(int(raw))) / 10 if raw >= 1 else 10 ** -len(f"{raw:.10f}".split(".")[1].rstrip("0"))
    for step in (1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10):
        if step * power >= raw:
            step *= power
            break
    return step * -(-top // step), step


def text(x, y, value, cls="ink", anchor="start", extra=""):
    return f'<text x="{x:.1f}" y="{y:.1f}" class="{cls}" text-anchor="{anchor}" {extra}>{escape(str(value))}</text>'


def hbar(x, y, width, height, cls, tip):
    """A bar from the baseline at x, square there and rounded 4px at its data end."""
    r = min(4, width / 2, height / 2)
    path = f"M{x:.1f},{y:.1f}H{x + width - r:.1f}A{r},{r} 0 0 1 {x + width:.1f},{y + r:.1f}V{y + height - r:.1f}A{r},{r} 0 0 1 {x + width - r:.1f},{y + height:.1f}H{x:.1f}Z"
    return f'<path d="{path}" class="{cls}"><title>{escape(tip)}</title></path>' if width > 0 else ""


def vbar(x, base, width, height, cls, tip):
    r = min(4, width / 2, height / 2)
    path = f"M{x:.1f},{base:.1f}V{base - height + r:.1f}A{r},{r} 0 0 1 {x + r:.1f},{base - height:.1f}H{x + width - r:.1f}A{r},{r} 0 0 1 {x + width:.1f},{base - height + r:.1f}V{base:.1f}Z"
    return f'<path d="{path}" class="{cls}"><title>{escape(tip)}</title></path>' if height > 0 else ""


def page(height, title, subtitle, body, label):
    return (
        f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {WIDTH} {height}" width="{WIDTH}" height="{height}" role="img" aria-label="{escape(label)}">'
        f"<title>{escape(title)}</title>{STYLE}<rect class=\"bg\" width=\"{WIDTH}\" height=\"{height}\"/>"
        + text(24, 30, title, "ink title")
        + text(24, 50, subtitle, "muted")
        + body
        + "</svg>\n"
    )


def bars(path, title, subtitle, rows, fmt, series=None, intervals=None, label_width=170):
    """Horizontal bars: rows of (label, value) or (label, value, second value), with an
    optional 95% interval per row as (low, high)."""
    top = max(max(r[1:]) if not intervals else max(i[1] for i in intervals) for r in rows) if not intervals else max(i[1] for i in intervals)
    top, step = nice(max(top, max(max(r[1:]) for r in rows)))
    left, right, band = 24 + label_width, WIDTH - 80, 22 if not series else 30
    y0 = 78 if series else 68
    scale = (right - left) / top
    body = []
    if series:
        for i, (name, cls) in enumerate(series):
            body += [f'<rect x="{left + i * 150}" y="58" width="12" height="12" rx="3" class="{cls}"/>', text(left + i * 150 + 18, 68, name, "muted")]
    height = y0 + band * len(rows) + 30
    for k in range(int(round(top / step)) + 1):
        x = left + k * step * scale
        body += [f'<line x1="{x:.1f}" x2="{x:.1f}" y1="{y0 - 4}" y2="{height - 26}" class="grid"/>', text(x, height - 10, fmt(k * step), "muted", "middle")]
    for n, row in enumerate(rows):
        y = y0 + n * band
        body.append(text(left - 8, y + band / 2 + 4, row[0], "ink", "end"))
        values = row[1:]
        thick = min(24, (band - 6) / len(values))
        for i, value in enumerate(values):
            cls = series[i][1] if series else "s1"
            body.append(hbar(left, y + 3 + i * (thick + 2), value * scale, thick, cls, f"{row[0]}: {fmt(value)}"))
        end = max(values) * scale
        if intervals:
            low, high = intervals[n]
            yc = y + 3 + thick / 2
            body += [f'<line x1="{left + low * scale:.1f}" x2="{left + high * scale:.1f}" y1="{yc:.1f}" y2="{yc:.1f}" class="whisker"/>',
                     f'<line x1="{left + low * scale:.1f}" x2="{left + low * scale:.1f}" y1="{yc - 5:.1f}" y2="{yc + 5:.1f}" class="whisker"/>',
                     f'<line x1="{left + high * scale:.1f}" x2="{left + high * scale:.1f}" y1="{yc - 5:.1f}" y2="{yc + 5:.1f}" class="whisker"/>']
            end = high * scale
        body.append(text(left + end + 6, y + band / 2 + 4, row[-1] if isinstance(row[-1], str) else " / ".join(fmt(v) for v in values), "muted"))
    path.write_text(page(height, title, subtitle, "".join(body), title))
    return path


def columns(path, title, subtitle, rows, fmt, marker=None):
    """Vertical columns: rows of (label, value, tooltip). marker, if given, is (index, label)
    for a hairline at a column, such as the median."""
    left, right, base, top_y = 70, WIDTH - 24, 300, 70
    top, step = nice(max(r[1] for r in rows))
    scale = (base - top_y) / top
    slot = (right - left) / len(rows)
    width = min(24, slot - 2)
    body = []
    for k in range(int(round(top / step)) + 1):
        y = base - k * step * scale
        body += [f'<line x1="{left}" x2="{right}" y1="{y:.1f}" y2="{y:.1f}" class="grid"/>', text(left - 8, y + 4, fmt(k * step), "muted", "end")]
    for i, (label, value, tip) in enumerate(rows):
        x = left + i * slot + (slot - width) / 2
        body.append(vbar(x, base, width, value * scale, "s1", tip))
        if len(rows) <= 12 or i % 2 == 0:
            body.append(text(x + width / 2, base + 16, label, "muted", "middle"))
    if marker:
        index, label = marker
        x = left + index * slot + slot / 2
        body += [f'<line x1="{x:.1f}" x2="{x:.1f}" y1="{top_y - 6}" y2="{base}" class="axis"/>', text(x + 4, top_y - 8, label, "ink")]
    body.append(f'<line x1="{left}" x2="{right}" y1="{base}" y2="{base}" class="axis"/>')
    path.write_text(page(base + 30, title, subtitle, "".join(body), title))
    return path


def years_chart(path, by_year):
    """Two panels on one time axis: articles per year, and candidates per million articles."""
    left, right = 70, WIDTH - 24
    first, last = by_year[0]["year"], by_year[-1]["year"]
    x = lambda year: left + (year - first) / (last - first) * (right - left)  # noqa: E731
    body = []
    panels = (
        ("Articles per year", "articles", 80, 230),
        ("Candidates per million articles", "candidates_per_million", 290, 440),
    )
    for name, key, top_y, base in panels:
        top, step = nice(max(r[key] for r in by_year))
        y = lambda v, top=top, top_y=top_y, base=base: base - v / top * (base - top_y)  # noqa: E731
        body.append(text(left, top_y - 10, name, "ink"))
        for k in range(int(round(top / step)) + 1):
            body += [f'<line x1="{left}" x2="{right}" y1="{y(k * step):.1f}" y2="{y(k * step):.1f}" class="grid"/>', text(left - 8, y(k * step) + 4, compact(k * step), "muted", "end")]
        runs, run = [], []
        for r in by_year:  # a gap in the years breaks the line
            if run and r["year"] != run[-1]["year"] + 1:
                runs.append(run)
                run = []
            run.append(r)
        runs.append(run)
        for run in runs:
            points = " ".join(f"{x(r['year']):.1f},{y(r[key]):.1f}" for r in run)
            if key == "articles" and len(run) > 1:
                body.append(f'<polygon class="wash" points="{x(run[0]["year"]):.1f},{base} {points} {x(run[-1]["year"]):.1f},{base}"/>')
            body.append(f'<polyline class="line" points="{points}"/>' if len(run) > 1 else f'<circle cx="{x(run[0]["year"]):.1f}" cy="{y(run[0][key]):.1f}" r="2" class="s1"/>')
        body.append(f'<line x1="{left}" x2="{right}" y1="{base}" y2="{base}" class="axis"/>')
    for r in by_year:  # hover targets, one per year across both panels
        tip = f"{r['year']}: {r['articles']:,} articles, {r['candidates']:,} candidates, {r['candidates_per_million']:.0f} per million"
        body.append(f'<rect class="hit" x="{x(r["year"]) - 2:.1f}" y="70" width="4" height="372"><title>{escape(tip)}</title></rect>')
    for year in range(1780, last + 1, 20):
        body.append(text(x(year), 460, year, "muted", "middle"))
    path.write_text(page(476, "Articles and candidates by year", "AmericanStories, all 180 year files; gaps are years with no file", "".join(body), "Articles and candidates by year"))
    return path


def draw_all(report, out):
    made = [years_chart(out / "years.svg", report["by_year"])]
    states = [s for s in report["by_state"] if s["articles"] >= 1_000_000]
    states.sort(key=lambda s: -s["candidates_per_million"])
    made.append(bars(out / "states.svg", "Candidates per million articles, by state",
                     f"States with a million articles or more; {report['no_state']['share_of_candidates']:.1%} of candidates have no state on record",
                     [("No state on record" if s["state"] == "unknown" else s["state"], s["candidates_per_million"]) for s in states], lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}"))
    terms = sorted(report["terms"]["any"], key=lambda t: -report["terms"]["any"][t])
    made.append(bars(out / "terms.svg", "Candidates by ghost term", "A candidate can hold several terms; 'only' counts those holding just this one",
                     [(t, report["terms"]["any"][t], report["terms"]["only"][t]) for t in terms], compact,
                     series=[("Holds the term", "s1"), ("Holds only this term", "s2")]))
    lengths = report["lengths"]["histogram"]
    made.append(columns(out / "lengths.svg", "Candidate length", f"Words in the article's text; median {report['lengths']['p50']}",
                        [(f"{b['from']}+" if b["to"] is None else f"{b['from']}–{b['to']}", b["candidates"], f"{b['candidates']:,} candidates") for b in lengths], compact))
    ocr = report["ocr_quality"]
    made.append(columns(out / "ocr.svg", "OCR quality of candidates", f"Share of words a standard dictionary knows; {ocr['sample']}",
                        [(f"{i * 5}%", n, f"{i * 5}–{i * 5 + 5}%: {n:,} candidates") for i, n in enumerate(ocr["histogram"])], compact,
                        marker=(min(19, int(ocr["p50"] * 20)), f"median {ocr['p50']:.0%}")))
    sizes = report["reprints"]["size_histogram"]
    made.append(columns(out / "reprints.svg", "Reprint clusters by size", f"{report['reprints']['clusters']:,} clusters hold {report['reprints']['clustered_candidates']:,} candidates ({report['reprints']['share_clustered']:.0%})",
                        [(f"{b['from']}+" if b["to"] is None else (f"{b['from']}" if b["from"] == b["to"] else f"{b['from']}–{b['to']}"), b["clusters"], f"{b['clusters']:,} clusters, {b['candidates']:,} candidates") for b in sizes], compact))
    composition = report["composition"].get("categories")
    if composition:
        rows = sorted(composition.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]["share"])

102	def draw(pools, sizes, n, seed):
103	    """n (year, item) pairs, each year drawn in proportion to its share of the pool across the

105	    equally. pools maps a year to its reservoir, and sizes to the pool's full size."""
106	    rng = random.Random(seed)
107	    years = sorted(year for year in pools if sizes.get(year) and pools[year])
108	    wanted = Counter(rng.choices(years, weights=[sizes[year] for year in years], k=n))
109	    return [
110	        (year, item)
111	        for year in years
112	        for item in rng.sample(list(pools[year]), min(wanted[year], len(pools[year])))
113	    ]

116	def uniform(counts, n, seed):

120	    picks = []
121	    for left in sorted(rng.sample(range(sum(counts.values())), n)):
122	        for year in years:
123	            if left < counts[year]:
124	                picks.append((year, left))
125	                break
126	            left -= counts[year]
127	    return picks

## Phase 2A (2026-10-29)

**19. Lexicon v1 counts the 1850s spirit noises as ghost terms, and reads through common OCR damage.**
- Only 3 of the 20 Stratford knockings articles of 1850 use a classic ghost word, and the walking skeleton's article uses none. So "knockings", "rappings" and "rappers" are ghost terms. A single "knocking", "spirits" and "strange noises" pu
- Each pattern takes the usual misreadings (long s as f, h as b or li, o as c or 0, t as l or 1, n as u), a lost i, and a word broken across a line with or without a hyphen. "spook" takes no c, because "spcck" is nearly always a misread spe
- Recall comes first. On faro_1850, v1 keeps 2,954 of 733,880 articles (`scripts/prefilter_year.py 1850`), and 18 of the 20 known knockings articles; the other 2 are in the near-miss pool.

**20. The knocking term stays: on its own it keeps 293 candidates of 1850, and 11 of the 18 known knockings articles.**
- A bare "knocking" was never a ghost term; it only marks a near-miss. The term is the plural "knockings", with its misreadings and line breaks (263 of the 293), and phrases such as "mysterious knocking" (30).
- Read in context, all 20 of a seeded sample of the 293 are about the spirit knockings: reports, debunkings, and two theatre bills. None is about a door or a fight.
- Without the term, 7 of the 18 known articles would survive. Later decades may use "knockings" for other things, and each year's samples will show it.

**21. The prefilter pre-checks folded stems, and keeps a 2,000-article sample of each pool per year.**
- Folding the OCR classes to one letter lets 34 short stems stand for every pattern, and an article holding none of them skips the regex. Over faro_1850 the pre-check changes no article's terms (`scripts/verify_precheck.py 1850`), and the y
- The near-miss pool and all non-candidates are each kept as a seeded reservoir of 2,000 articles per year, in `data/samples/{year}.jsonl.zst`: 4.8 MB for 1850.

**22. The ingest runs each year in a fresh process, and a year is done once its manifest is written.**
- A year's prefilter is CPU-bound Python, so four years in one process would share a core under the GIL. The worker runs the year activity in a pool of four processes, a fresh one for each year, which also gives every year its own peak memo
- Outputs go to partial files that are renamed once complete, and the manifest is written last. A year is skipped when its manifest's lexicon and code versions match the current ones. The code version is a hash of the modules that shape the
- A year that fails all five attempts is listed with its reason, and the other years carry on.
- 1804, 1850 and 1910 took 2.7 s, 50.6 s and 389.4 s, wrote 39 MB in all, and peaked at 536 MB of memory (1910). A second run of 1850 wrote byte-identical counts. The code version hashes exact bytes, so even a reformat re-runs a year: forma

**23. A year is skipped only while its cache key and every output's hash match, and a lost attempt stops at its next heartbeat.**
- The cache key is the dataset revision, the lexicon version and the code version. The ingest reads AmericanStories at its 2025-03-26 commit, `77e27fa6`, instead of `main`, so a cached year's input can't change under it.
- Manifests and counts are in git, but candidates and samples are not, so a fresh clone skipped every year and had no candidates. Each manifest now records every output's sha256, and a year is skipped only when every output on disk matches.
- The tarballs are never cached (decision 3): 340 GB won't fit on the disk, and a full re-read costs about 75 minutes and nothing else.
- Two attempts at one year can run at once. A timed-out attempt keeps going after Temporal starts its retry, and a spawn-pool child outlives a worker killed with SIGKILL and still writes its files. So partial files are named for their proce
- In the tests, a cancel reaches a year only through `is_cancelled()`, as in the process pool. Otherwise the SDK would interrupt the test's thread for it.
- The code is frozen while the full archive runs. The lexicon, prefilter, stream and year modules make up the code version, and a restarted worker replays the workflow's history against the workflow code.

**24. Temporal identities name the process and its role, not the host.**
The SDK's default identity is `pid@hostname`, and Temporal keeps it in every workflow's history, which the kill test's screenshots show. Like Sentry's `server_name` (decision 15), the worker, `make ingest` and `make smoke` use `pid@papergho

**25. The full read ran four years at a time, each on one CPU-bound core. A re-read can set its concurrency from these numbers.**
- All 180 year files, 340.4 GB at revision `77e27fa6`, took 118.6 min on 2026-10-30: an aggregate 47.8 MB/s. Every manifest's `bytes_read` equals the listed size, no year failed, and no partial file was left.
- 370,313,913 articles gave 1,050,459 candidates. The outputs take 1.94 GB (candidates 1.34 GB, samples 0.59 GB), and the highest peak memory was 535 MB (1910).
- Each year process is CPU-bound on one core: 12.8 MB/s at the median over the 87 years above 1 GB, with a range of 11.0–15.6. With four running, the network carried 55 MB/s at the median of minute samples (50–57 for the middle 80%), an
- Concurrency stayed at four:
  - Time isn't the constraint.
  - One clean run gives one wall time and clean kill-test evidence.
  - Eight CPU-bound processes would saturate the owner's laptop while they use it, for well short of 2×, because 6 of its 10 cores are efficiency cores.
- Six years ran twice:
  - The streams for 1872 and 1889 ended partway through a page (`tarfile.ReadError: unexpected end of data`).
  - Kill test 1's SIGKILL cost 1881–1884 their first attempts (`eval/results/phase2a/kill-test-1.md`).
  - Each retry read its whole file again, because a gzip stream can't seek.
- 1850 reproduces. With its candidates file moved aside, a rerun wrote all three outputs byte-identical, with the same sha256 as the committed manifest.

**26. Crops are one per box, fetched once and cached, and the display headline drops only the masthead lines that lead it.**
- There is one IIIF crop per box in `bbox_list`, in its order, which is the reading order. This replaces decision 18's single crop over every box, which takes in the columns between them on a multi-column article. In 64 of 595 multi-box 185
- Requests to the Library of Congress:
  - They go at most one a second, with a User-Agent that names the project.
  - A busy answer is retried after 5 s, then 20 s. tile.loc.gov answered a region it hadn't made yet with a 503 after 35 s, and served the same URL a minute later in 0.2 s.
  - Crops are cached under `data/crops/`, keyed by URL, and a reply that isn't an image is never cached.
- A batch path can name a batch that LoC has since reissued. Two of the crop check's pages are recorded in `ver01` batches that tile.loc.gov no longer serves, and loc.gov lists them under `ver02`. So when a crop from a batch path is missing
- The display headline:
  - Leading lines are dropped while they are the paper's title, its own place and state, an issue date, or a numbered volume or issue line. Lines of rules and stray marks are dropped anywhere.
  - A weekday or month alone isn't a date line, an issue word needs a number, and a title or place under 6 letters must stand alone as a word.
  - The stored OCR is untouched.
- Precision, judged by hand on 200 dropped lines sampled with a fixed seed from candidate headlines (`scripts/headline_drops.py`):
  - The first rule dropped such lines anywhere, and 142 of its 200 drops were correct (71.0%, 95% interval 64.4–76.8%). It took dates and words that belonged to the article, as in "Out Ghosts Next / Monday Evening".
  - The final rule's precision is 195 of 200 (97.5%, 94.3–98.9%), and 139 of the 143 lines with letters (97.2%, 93.0–98.9%).
  - The final rule drops 10,287 lines instead of 17,270. The cost is masthead blocks whose title line came out garbled, which now stay in the headline.
- The crop check (`eval/results/phase2a/crop-check.md`): 48 of 50 candidates pass (96%, 95% interval 86.5–98.9%). The two failures:
  - One page has no IIIF service: loc.gov has no item for the 1964 Arizona Tribune.
  - One article's first box, as AmericanStories gives it, is the last line of the item above.

# Step 2A.5: DONE

Commit `10435e1` on `phase-2a-archive`, pushed. The PR is held until the 2A gate. Decision 26 records the design and the numbers.

## Crop check: 48 of 50 pass (96%, 95% Wilson interval 86.5–98.9%)

`eval/results/phase2a/crop-check.md` has a verdict and a reason for each pick. The contact sheet is `crop-check-1.jpg` to `crop-check-5.jpg`, and the picks are in `crop-check.json`.

- **Picks:** one per year, from 50 years evenly spread over the 173 years with candidates (1770–1964), drawn at random with a per-year fixed seed. They come from 45 LoC batches, with at most 2 from any one, and have 105 boxes in all.
- **Pass means:** the crops, one per box in `bbox_list` order, show the article's OCR text from its first line, in reading order, with nothing missing.
- **Failures:**
  - **#21, 1862 Daily dispatch:** box 1 is the last line of the item above, a letter's address and signature ("To Hon. W. H. Seward … Franklin Pierce"). The article's OCR doesn't contain it, so AmericanStories gave the article a stray box.
  - **#50, 1964 Arizona tribune:** there is no crop. The scan has no batch path, and loc.gov lists the title (Phoenix, 1958–197?) but has no item for 1964-11-06, so no IIIF service can be named.
- **Saved by the reissued-batch fallback:** #2 (1796) and #16 (1845) are recorded in `ver01` batches that tile.loc.gov no longer serves (404), and loc.gov lists them under `ver02`. Without the fallback, 4 picks would have failed.
- **Notes on passes**, all of them with the crop matching the OCR:
  - Overlapping boxes repeat a line in 7 picks.
  - Box edges clip a first or last letter as the OCR does in 5.
  - 3 articles start mid-story, where AmericanStories split them.
  - In 3, a box runs into the next item.
  - Box 1 is the paper's own dateline in #15, an ornament in #2, and a sliver of the item above in #33.

## Display-headline precision, judged by hand (`headline-drops*.json`)

- **First rule** (masthead lines dropped anywhere): 142 of 200 correct, **71.0% (64.4–76.8%)**, out of 17,270 drops in candidate headlines. The 58 mis-drops:
  - about 41 dates or times that belong to the article, such as "Out Ghosts Next / Monday Evening", "TUESDAY, OCTOBER 31 / WILL BE HALLOWEEN", listing days, and poems titled MARCH and EVENING
  - 9 lone issue words or series numbers ("World / Series", "CHRISTMAS / NUMBER.")
  - 3 times the paper's name or place inside a sentence ("in Big Stone Gap.")
  - 5 figures from tables or ads
- **The rule change:**
  - Masthead lines are dropped only while they lead the headline. Rules and stray marks are dropped anywhere.
  - A weekday or month needs a second date word, a number or the paper's name.
  - An issue word needs a number.
- **Final rule:** 10,287 drops. A fresh seeded sample of 200 had 195 correct, **97.5% (94.3–98.9%)**. On the 143 lines with letters it's 139 correct, **97.2% (93.0–98.9%)**.
  - The 5 mis-drops: a column title "IN DETROIT", a story's opening year "1773.", an advertisement's own date, an essay series' "NO. XXXVI." and "SATURDAY [Night Sermons]".
  - The cost: masthead blocks whose title line OCR'd garbled now keep their date lines. That's 27 of the 142 correct drops in the first sample.
- **Short names:** a title or place under 6 letters must stand alone as a word. Real cases:
  - `PoStry` (Poetry) in The post, and `VIOLA` in The Iola register, were mis-drops before.
  - The Sun's own masthead `THE SUN, SUNDAY. DECEMBER 9. 1891.` was missed before, because "sun" was taken out of SUNDAY.
  - Star and Bee had no such line in their own papers, so their tests use real lines from other papers (`Stars.`, `BEER.`).
  - Tests fail if every name is bounded (Dallas, Memphis) or none is (the five short-name cases).

# Step 2A.6: DONE

Commit `ba247a0` on `phase-2a-archive`, pushed. The PR is held until the 2A gate. Decision 27 has the method, the category definitions and the numbers.

`make eval` runs `scripts/eval_a.py`. In 41 s it writes `eval/results/eval_a.json` and eight charts to `eval/results/eval_a/`. The samples are seeded, and a rerun keeps the hand judgments in `composition.json`, `recall.json` and `reprint-check.json`.

## Headline numbers

- 370,313,913 articles in 16,887,460 pages gave 1,050,459 candidates (2,837 per million) and 6,872,539 near-miss articles.
- No state: 11.2% of candidates (and 11.2% of their share of articles; see `no_state` in the JSON).
- Candidate length: the median is 358 words.
- OCR quality: the median is 92.7% of words of 3+ letters in `/usr/share/dict/words`. It is measured on 1 candidate in 20, chosen by the CRC of its id; 51,718 of those have 20 words or more. `median_by_decade` is in the JSON.
- Reprints:
  - 80,770 clusters hold 330,158 candidates (31.4%), which leaves 801,071 distinct stories. 71,191 clusters span more than one paper.
  - The hand check found 20 of 20 sampled pairs to be the same story.
  - The largest clusters are syndicated patent-medicine ads (684, 402, 379 and 308 printings), a book ad (487) and a steamer schedule (271).
  - Linking on one shared run chained 6,720 candidates together through Bible verses, so the final method needs two shared runs.

## Composition (200 candidates, drawn uniformly at random, judged by hand)

| Category | n | Share (95% Wilson) | Implied candidates |
|---|---|---|---|
| figurative | 79 | 39.5% (33.0–46.4%) | 414,900 |
| fiction | 47 | 23.5% (18.2–29.8%) | 246,900 |
| name or title | 30 | 15.0% (10.7–20.6%) | 157,600 |
| other | 23 | 11.5% (7.8–16.7%) | 120,800 |
| religious | 10 | 5.0% (2.7–9.0%) | 52,500 |
| **ghost report** | **7** | **3.5% (1.7–7.0%)** | **36,800 (17,900–74,000)** |
| social event | 4 | 2.0% (0.8–5.0%) | 21,000 |

- **A ghost report** is a ghost, haunting, apparition or spirit manifestation, told as something that happened or was claimed to. A ghost scare that turns out to be a trapped man counts. Witches, a séance advertised for later and essays doubting ghosts don't. The other categories are defined in decision 27.
- **The 7 reports:**
  - 1854: a voice taken for Phie's ghost, which was a trapped man.
  - 1875: an Englishwoman executed for witchcraft, whose ghost is believed to haunt the spot.
  - 1878: Vanderbilt's dead wife speaking through the medium Foster, in will-case testimony.
  - 1904: a defendant who points at a spectre in court.
  - 1911: Anne Boleyn's headless coach at Blickling.
  - 1911: lights in a cemetery, and a party that went to investigate.
  - 1916: the American legation in Peking, haunted by an officer killed in the Boxer massacres.
- **OCR accidents:** 15 of the 200 are OCR misreads in the source text, such as "flaunting" printed as "haunting" (6), "wrappings" as "rappings" (2) and a codling moth as a goblin moth. The lexicon matches what the OCR says, so only the reader can reject them. They are in "other".
- **Sizes:**
  - The reader's job is 1,050,459 candidates, or 801,071 if it reads one printing per cluster. About 96.5% of them are not reports.
  - Atlas would hold about 22,300 ghost-report stories, counting each candidate as 1/k of a story when its cluster has k printings. That figure is rough: 3 of the 7 reports were reprinted, in clusters of 7, 13 and 30.
  - The sample's clustered share is 49 of 200, against 31.4% overall. That's within chance, but at its edge.

## Recall

The samples come from the seeded reservoirs of 2,000 articles per year, with each year weighted by its pool's size across the archive. The verdicts are in `recall.json`.

| Pool | Ghost reports | Rate (95% Wilson) | Implied articles |
|---|---|---|---|
| Near-miss (6,872,539) | 0 of 300 | 0%, at most 1.26% | at most 86,900 |
| All non-candidates (369,263,454) | 0 of 300 | 0%, at most 1.26% | at most 4.67 million |

- The near-miss sample's terms were spirit (210), knock (80), supernatural (4), spiritualism (4), rap (3) and seance (3). It is mostly school spirit, spirits as liquor, and knocks on doors and in fights.
- There were two closest calls, neither counted:
  - Near-miss #74, from 1881, is an announcement of séances in which spirits "will materialize". It's a show to come, not an occurrence.
  - Near-miss #111, from 1892, is "Is She a Witch?", about a Kentucky girl who claims to be a witch. It is supernatural, but there's no ghost.
- 9 of the 300 random articles hold any word from eval A's flag list. They are spirits in medicine and liquor ads, the spirit of brotherly love, a Billy the Kid narrative, Cleek detective fiction, a Bible verse and a French news item. None is a report.
- **The random bound is loose:** 4.67 million is 127 times the 36,800 reports found. Bounding the misses at the number found (recall of 50% or more) takes about 38,600 random articles with none among them. """The headline as the site shows it: the OCR's headline without the masthead lines that an
article's first box often takes in, which lead it. The stored OCR keeps them."""

import html
import re

# a weekday or month, and a time of day, as a masthead's dateline prints them
DATE_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday|january|february"
    r"|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december|jan|feb"
    r"|mar|apr|jun|jul|aug|sept?|oct|nov|dec)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
TIMES = re.compile(r"\b(?:morning|evening)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
ISSUE_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:new|series|vol|volume|no|number|whole|page)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)
# numbers as printed and as OCR misreads them (I or l for 1, O for 0), and roman numerals
NUMERALS = re.compile(r"\b(?:[\dIilOo]+|[IVXLCDM]+)\b")


def letters(text):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", text.lower())


def spelled(word):
    """These letters with anything but letters between them, since OCR splits a
    masthead's wide lettering: 'portland' matches 'PORTL AND'."""
    return r"[\W\d_]*".join(map(re.escape, word))


def names(paper):
    """The paper's title, with or without 'The', and its place with or without its state,
    from the LoC title: 'The national era. [volume] (Washington [D.C.]) 1847-1860' gives
    national era, and Washington or Washington D.C."""
    paper = html.unescape(paper or "")
    title = letters(paper.split("[")[0].split("(")[0]).removeprefix("the")
    found = []
    if title:
        found.append(alone(rf"(?:{spelled('the')}[\W\d_]*)?{spelled(title)}", title))
    place = re.search(r"\(\[?([^,\[\])]+)[,\s\[]*([^\])]*)", paper)
    if place and letters(place[1]):
        state = letters(place[2])
        state = rf"(?:[\W\d_]*{spelled(state)})?" if state else ""
        found.append(alone(spelled(letters(place[1])) + state, letters(place[1])))
    return [re.compile(name, re.IGNORECASE) for name in found]


def alone(pattern, name):
    """A short name must stand alone: 'post' is inside 'PoStry' (Poetry) and 'iola' inside
    'VIOLA'. A longer one needn't, since OCR runs stray letters into mastheads
    ('NMEMPHIs') and a line still needs all but two of its letters accounted for."""
    return rf"(?<![a-z]){pattern}(?![a-z])" if len(name) < 6 else pattern


def masthead(line, paper_names):
    """A line with no letters, or one that is the paper's names, a date or a numbered issue
    line, give or take numbers and two stray letters. A weekday or month alone isn't a date
    (it heads listings, and poems are named for months), unless the paper's name is beside
    it; an issue word needs a number; and numbers alone don't count ('II' is a part)."""
    if not letters(line):
        return True
    rest, found = line, False
    for pattern in paper_names:
        rest, matches = pattern.subn(" ", rest)
        found = found or matches > 0
    numbered = bool(re.search(r"\d", rest) or NUMERALS.search(rest))
    dates = len(DATE_WORDS.findall(rest))
    times = len(TIMES.findall(rest)) if dates else 0
    if dates + times >= 2 or (dates and (numbered or found)):
        rest, found = TIMES.sub(" ", DATE_WORDS.sub(" ", rest)), True
    if numbered and ISSUE_WORDS.search(rest):
        rest, found = ISSUE_WORDS.sub(" ", rest), True
    return found and len(letters(NUMERALS.sub(" ", rest))) <= 2


def masthead_lines(headline, paper):
    """Each line of the headline that isn't blank, and whether the site drops it. Masthead
    lines go only while they lead: a dated line further down belongs to the article ('Out
    Ghosts Next / Monday Evening'). Rules and stray marks go anywhere."""
    paper_names, leading = names(paper), True
    for line in (headline or "").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        marks = not letters(line) and not re.search(r"\d", line)
        if marks or (leading and masthead(line, paper_names)):
            yield line, True
        else:
            leading = False
            yield line, False


def display_headline(headline, paper):
    return "\n".join(
        line for line, dropped in masthead_lines(headline, paper) if not dropped
    )

import datetime

    r"|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december|jan|feb"
    r"|mar|apr|jun|jul|aug|sept?|oct|nov|dec)\b",

)

)

  - Each weekday and month on the line must be the issue's.
  - The issue's weekday then settles it, because OCR misreads digits far more often than words. The Sun's `SUNDAY. DECEMBER 9.` is its masthead of the 6th.
  - Without a weekday, the day after a month and the year must be the issue's too, with OCR's I, l and O read as digits. So an advertisement's `April 4th.` in the issue of the 11th stays, as does a story's `1773.`.
- `In` followed by the paper's own place is never a masthead (`IN DETROIT` titles a column).
- A number line goes only when the leading lines hold the paper's title or its volume. This covers a bare number, and `No.`, `Number`, `Whole No.` or `Page` with a number, because `NO. XXXVI.` on its own numbers an essay.
- Rerun on the same 200 judged lines (`scripts/headline_drops.py --same`):

That's 22 issue numbers with neither the title nor the volume beside them (`NO. 40`, `NUMBER 81.`), 5 whole numbers, 3 rules with a stray digit, 4 datelines with no weekday whose digits OCR misread (`DELAWARE, OHIO, AUGUST 4, 1866.` for 1865), and 3 datelines whose weekday or month isn't the record's.

- 335,907 candidates (32.0%) have a scan with no batch path, so the IIIF service for their page has to come from somewhere other than `raw_data_loc`. The count for each year is in `eval_a.json` (`by_year[].no_batch_path`). By decade the share runs from 15% in the 1820s to 37% in the 1850s, and stays between 24% and 36% from the 1840s on.

# 2A.5 follow-ups: DONE

Commit `9d56340` on `phase-2a-archive`, pushed. It follows eval A's `ba247a0`. The PR is still held until the 2A gate. Decisions 28 and 29 have the detail.

## 1. The last five headline mis-drops

**The rule** (`paperghosts/ingest/headline.py`). `display_headline` and `masthead_lines` now take the record's edition date.

- **Datelines:**
  - Each weekday and month on the line must be the issue's.
  - The issue's weekday then settles it, because OCR misreads digits far more often than words. The Sun's `SUNDAY. DECEMBER 9.` is its masthead of the 6th.
  - Without a weekday, the day after a month and the year must also be the issue's, with I, l and O read as digits.
  - A line of only numbers holding a year must hold the issue's year.
- **`In` followed by the paper's place** is never a masthead.
- **Number lines** go only when the leading lines hold the paper's title or a `Vol.` line. That covers a bare number, and `No.`, `Number`, `Whole No.` or `Page` with a number.

**On the same 200 judged lines** (`uv run python scripts/headline_drops.py --same`):

- Mis-drops still made: **0 of 5**.
- Correct drops lost: **37 of 195**:
  - 22 numbers with neither the title nor a volume beside them (`NO. 40`, `NUMBER 81.`, `No. 36.`, a bare `2` and `81`)
  - 5 `WHOLE NO.` lines
  - 3 lines of stray marks with a digit (`*%%~*+<<%+***~%~4 #`)
  - 4 datelines with no weekday whose digits don't match the record's: `DELAWARE, OHIO, AUGUST 4, 1866.` (issue 1865-08-04), `September 6. 1905.` (09-08), `RICHMOND, SEPTEMBER 90. I8e5.` and `MONTPELIER, DECEMBER 20, 1871.` (issue 1841)
  - 3 datelines whose weekday or month isn't the record's: `SATURDAY, March 16'` in a Thursday 14th issue, `THURSDAY MORNING, MAY ?, 1870` in a June 2 issue, and `Friday. July ~.` in a Saturday issue
- Precision on the 158 lines still dropped: 158 of 158 (95% Wilson interval 97.6–100%).
- **Over every candidate headline:** 7,509 drops, down from 10,287, and **none that the old rule kept** (checked by running both rules). So the 158 remain a fair sample of the new drops.
  - Of the 2,778 lines no longer dropped, split as in the sample, about 2,450 are masthead lines left showing, or 0.2% of candidates.
  - About 330 are headline lines no longer hidden.

**Interpretation calls, all yours to overrule:**
- **"Matches the issue's own date, year or weekday."** I read it as: no weekday or month may contradict the issue, and a matching weekday settles the line. Requiring every digit to match as well keeps the same 0 mis-drops but loses 54 correct drops instead of 37. The extra 17 are datelines such as `THURSDAY MORNING. JULY 10, 1877.` in the Thursday 19th issue.
- **`WHOLE NO.` follows your number-line rule.** Counting it with the volume would win back 5, with no mis-drop in the sample.
- **Place lines don't count as "the title"** for a number line.

**Tests** (`tests/test_headline.py`, 45 real cases, all now passing the issue date):
- The 5 mis-drops are keeps.
- New drops: a whole number beside the title (Indiana State sentinel, 1863), a page number beside the title (Blue-grass blade, 1908), a weekday settling a misread day (Detroit times `Saturday. July 80.`, 1910), and the issue's year alone (`1900.`).
- Four old drops are now keeps, by design: two whole numbers alone, the National Era's misread dateline, and the Portland gazette's Saturday in an issue that LoC dates to a Tuesday.

The callers `crop_check.py`, `load_skeleton.py` and `headline_drops.py` pass the date. The skeleton's stored headline comes out the same under the new rule (its `New Series-VOl. 4-NO. 40.` is a volume line), so Atlas needs no reload.

## 2. Missing scans

- **335,907 candidates (32.0%) have no batch path.** `eval_a.json` has the totals in `totals.no_batch_path` and `share_no_batch_path`, and each year in `by_year[].no_batch_path`. `make eval` prints it too.
  - By decade: 15% in the 1820s and 18% in the 1830s, then 29–37% from the 1840s to the 1910s, peaking at 37% in the 1850s. From the 1920s on it is 24–28%.
  - The largest yearly counts are 1909–1914, at about 6,600–7,000 a year.
- **Not every one of them is a lost clipping.**
  - In the crop check, loc.gov named the IIIF service for 12 of the 13 picks with no batch path. The 13th was #50.
  - Offline, these candidates sit on 283,546 pages and 19,115 reels. **92.4% of them are on a reel whose batch another candidate's batch path names.** The service is `batch + LCCN + reel + issue + seq`, so it can be built without any lookup.
  - That leaves **25,595 candidates (2.4% of all) on 1,292 reels** needing loc.gov, one lookup per reel.
  - 220 reels hold more than one batch: 57 are a batch and its reissue, and 163 are split between batches. So a reel-to-batch map needs a crop check before we trust it. It isn't built.
  - At the ghost-report rate, that's roughly 900 reports needing a lookup, and an unknown share of those with no clipping at all.
- **loc.gov rate limit, my mistake:**
  - loc.gov's JSON API allows **20 requests a minute** and blocks for **an hour** past that ([Working Within Limits](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/working-within-limits/)). Image services allow 150.
  - The crop code throttled everything to one a second.
  - I ran a 100-page lookup probe at that rate, and it got 429s at 04:03. This machine is likely blocked from loc.gov's JSON API until about 05:03. tile.loc.gov wasn't touched afterwards.
  - Fix: `crops.get` now spaces www.loc.gov requests 3.5 s apart, with a test.
  - The probe script is deleted, because a reel-based check is the better probe.
  - Per-page lookups for all 283,546 pages would take 11.5 days at that rate, so the site can't resolve them on demand.
- **Crop 21's stray box** is recorded in decision 29 as a known limitation, with no fix.

## Suggested next

In 2B (storage and loading), build the reel-to-batch map from the batch paths in candidates and samples. Crop-check a seeded sample of the services it infers, through tile.loc.gov info.json (150 a minute). Then look up the remaining ~1,292 reels at 17 a minute, about 75 minutes.

84	def known(word, words):
85	    if word in words:
86	        return True
87	    return any(
88	        len(word) > len(end) + 2
89	        and word.endswith(end)
90	        and word[: -len(end)] + back in words
91	        for end, back in ENDINGS
92	    )

95	def ocr_quality(text, words, least=20):
96	    """The share of the article's words of three letters or more that the dictionary knows,
97	    once line-break hyphens are joined and common endings come off; None under `least`."""
98	    found = WORD.findall((text or "").replace("-\n", "").lower())
99	    if len(found) < least:
100	        return None
101	    return sum(known(word, words) for word in found) / len(found)

104	def draw(pools, sizes, n, seed):
105	    """n (year, item) pairs, each year drawn in proportion to its share of the pool across the
106	    archive, so the sample stands for every article in the pool rather than for each year
107	    equally. pools maps a year to its reservoir, and sizes to the pool's full size."""
108	    rng = random.Random(seed)
109	    years = sorted(year for year in pools if sizes.get(year) and pools[year])
110	    wanted = Counter(rng.choices(years, weights=[sizes[year] for year in years], k=n))
111	    return [
112	        (year, item)
113	        for year in years
114	        for item in rng.sample(list(pools[year]), min(wanted[year], len(pools[year])))
115	    ]

118	def uniform(counts, n, seed):
119	    """n (year, index) pairs without replacement, every candidate equally likely."""
120	    rng = random.Random(seed)
121	    years = sorted(counts)
122	    picks = []
123	    for left in sorted(rng.sample(range(sum(counts.values())), n)):
124	        for year in years:
125	            if left < counts[year]:
126	                picks.append((year, left))
127	                break
128	            left -= counts[year]
129	    return picks

247	def rate(hits, n, of):
248	    low, high = wilson(hits, n)
249	    return {
250	        "count": hits,
251	        "n": n,
252	        "share": hits / n,
253	        "low": low,
254	        "high": high,
255	        "implied": round(hits / n * of),
256	        "implied_low": round(low * of),
257	        "implied_high": round(high * of),
258	    }

"""The prefilter's pass over one year: the candidates, their term counts, and fixed-size
samples of the non-candidates, which measure its recall (ARCHITECTURE section 3.1)."""

import os
import random
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

import orjson
import zstandard

from paperghosts.ingest.lexicon import ghost_terms, near_miss_terms

SAMPLE_SIZE = 2000


class Reservoir:
    """A uniform sample of fixed size from a stream of unknown length (Algorithm R)."""

    def __init__(self, size, rng):
        self.size, self.rng, self.seen, self.items = size, rng, 0, []

    def offer(self, item):
        if len(self.items) < self.size:
            self.items.append(item)
        else:
            slot = self.rng.randrange(self.seen + 1)
            if slot < self.size:
                self.items[slot] = item
        self.seen += 1


def record(member, page, article, **found):
    lccn = page.get("lccn") or {}
    return {
        "member": member,
        "article_id": article.get("id"),
        "lccn": lccn.get("lccn"),
        "paper": lccn.get("title"),
        "state": lccn.get("state"),
        "date": (page.get("edition") or {}).get("date"),
        "scan": page.get("scan"),
        "headline": article.get("headline"),
        "text": article.get("article"),
        "bbox_list": article.get("bbox_list"),
        **found,
    }


def scan(pages, year, sample_size=SAMPLE_SIZE):
    """Sorts every article of one year into candidates, the near-miss pool and the rest,
    keeping seeded reservoir samples of the near-miss pool and of all non-candidates."""
    random_sample = Reservoir(sample_size, random.Random(f"{year} random"))
    near_miss_sample = Reservoir(sample_size, random.Random(f"{year} near-miss"))
    result = {"pages": 0, "articles": 0, "near_miss": 0, "candidates": []}
    per_term, only, spellings = Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
    by_state = defaultdict(lambda: {"pages": 0, "articles": 0, "candidates": 0})
    for member, page in pages:
        result["pages"] += 1
        state = by_state[(page.get("lccn") or {}).get("state") or "unknown"]
        state["pages"] += 1
        for article in page.get("full articles") or []:
            result["articles"] += 1
            state["articles"] += 1
            text = f"{article.get('headline') or ''}\n{article.get('article') or ''}"
            terms = ghost_terms(text)
            if terms:
                state["candidates"] += 1
                result["candidates"].append(record(member, page, article, terms=terms))
                per_term.update(terms.keys())
                only.update(terms.keys() if len(terms) == 1 else ())
                spellings.update(
                    (t, form) for t, forms in terms.items() for form in forms
                )
                continue
            near = near_miss_terms(text)
            item = record(member, page, article, near_miss_terms=near)
            random_sample.offer(item)
            if near:
                result["near_miss"] += 1
                near_miss_sample.offer(item)
    result.update(
        per_term=per_term, only=only, spellings=spellings, by_state=dict(by_state)
    )
    result["samples"] = {
        "random": random_sample.items,
        "near_miss": near_miss_sample.items,
    }
    return result


def write_jsonl_zst(path, records):
    """Writes the records to a partial file first, so a crash never leaves a short one."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # named for its process: a timed-out attempt may still be writing beside its retry
    partial = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial")
    with zstandard.open(partial, "wb") as out:
        for item in records:
            out.write(orjson.dumps(item) + b"\n")
    partial.replace(path)
"""The prefilter's lexicons: ghost terms that make an article a candidate, and near-miss
terms that put an article without one into the recall pool (ARCHITECTURE section 3.1).

Each pattern takes the common OCR misreadings: long s read as f, h as b or li, o as c or 0,
t as l or 1, and n as u. Recall comes first; triage and the reader handle precision.
"""

import re

VERSION = "v1"

GHOST = {
    "ghost": r"[gq](?:h|b|li)[oc0][sf][tl1i](?:s|ly|-?like)?",
    "apparition": r"ap?par[il1][tl1i][il1][oc0][nu]s?",
    "spectre": r"[sf]p[ec]c[tl1](?:r[ec]s?|[ec]rs?|ral)",
    "phantom": r"(?:p[hb]|f)a[nu][tl1](?:[oc0](?:m|rn|in)|asm)s?",
    "haunt": r"[hb]a[uon][nu][tl1](?:ed|ing|s)?",
    "spook": r"[sf]p[o0]{2}k(?:s|y|ed)?",  # not c: "spcck" is nearly always a misread speck
    "wraith": r"wra[il1][tl1][hb]s?",
    "poltergeist": r"po[l1i][tl1]erge[il1][sf][tl1]s?",
    "banshee": r"ban[sf]hees?",
    "goblin": r"(?:hob)?gobl[il1]ns?",
    # the 1850s spirit noises: most Stratford knockings reports use no ghost word at all.
    # The i may be lost, and the word may break across a line with no hyphen ("knock\nings").
    "knocking": (
        r"k[nu][oc0][ce]k(?:\s*\n\s*)?(?:[il1]?(?:n|u|y|ri)|m)gs"
        r"|(?:mysterious|strange|spirit|unaccountable)[\s-]+k[nu][oc0]ck(?:ing|s)"
    ),
    "rapping": (
        r"rapp(?:\s*\n\s*)?[il1]?(?:n|u|ri)gs|rappers|[sf]pirit[\s-]+rapp(?:ing|er)s?"
    ),
}

NEAR_MISS = {
    "knock": r"k[nu][oc0]ck(?:s|ed|ing)?",
    "rap": r"rapp(?:ing|ed)",
    "noise": r"(?:strange|mysterious|unaccountable|unearthly|unnatural)[\s-]+(?:noise|sound)s?",
    "spirit": r"[sf]pirits?",
    "spiritualism": r"[sf]piritual(?:ism|ists?)",
    "seance": r"s[eé]ances?",
    "supernatural": r"[sf]upernatural",
}


def _matcher(terms):
    alternatives = "|".join(f"(?P<{term}>{pattern})" for term, pattern in terms.items())
    return re.compile(rf"\b(?:{alternatives})\b", re.IGNORECASE)


GHOST_MATCHER, NEAR_MISS_MATCHER = _matcher(GHOST), _matcher(NEAR_MISS)

# The pre-check folds most OCR confusion classes above to one letter (q→g, b→h, c 0→o,
# f→s, i 1 t→l, u→n). Every match of a term then contains one of its stems, so an article
# with none of them can skip the regex. Stems are long enough to pass over the commonest
# lookalikes in 1850: "throughout" (gho), "sarsaparilla" (aparll) and "annual" (nnnal).
FOLD = str.maketrans("qbc0fi1tu", "ghoosllln")
GHOST_STEMS = {
    "ghost": ("ghos", "gllos"),
    "apparition": ("parlllo",),
    "spectre": ("speolr", "speoler", "speolor", "spoolr", "spooler", "spoolor"),
    "phantom": ("phanl", "sanlo", "sanlas"),
    "haunt": ("hannl", "haonl"),
    "spook": ("spook",),
    "wraith": ("wrall",),
    "poltergeist": ("pollerg",),
    "banshee": ("hansh",),
    "goblin": ("gohll",),
    "knocking": ("knook", "knoek"),
    "rapping": ("rapp",),
}
NEAR_MISS_STEMS = {
    "knock": ("knook",),
    "rap": ("rapp",),
    "noise": ("slrang", "mysler", "nnaooo", "nnearl", "nnnalnr"),
    "spirit": ("splrl",),
    "spiritualism": ("splrl",),
    "seance": ("seano", "séano"),
    "supernatural": ("snpern",),
}


_GHOST_STEMS = tuple(stem for group in GHOST_STEMS.values() for stem in group)
_NEAR_MISS_STEMS = tuple(stem for group in NEAR_MISS_STEMS.values() for stem in group)


def _find(matcher, stems, text, precheck):
    text = text.replace("-\n", "")  # rejoin words hyphenated at a line end
    if precheck:
        folded = text.lower().translate(FOLD)
        if not any(stem in folded for stem in stems):
            return {}
    found = {}
    for match in matcher.finditer(text):
        form = " ".join(match.group().lower().split())
        found.setdefault(match.lastgroup, set()).add(form)
    return {term: sorted(forms) for term, forms in found.items()}


def ghost_terms(text, precheck=True):
    """Each ghost term in the text, with the spellings it was scanned as."""
    return _find(GHOST_MATCHER, _GHOST_STEMS, text, precheck)


def near_miss_terms(text, precheck=True):
    """Each near-miss term in the text, with the spellings it was scanned as."""
    return _find(NEAR_MISS_MATCHER, _NEAR_MISS_STEMS, text, precheck)

"""Eval A's helpers: OCR quality as the share of words a dictionary knows, and samples that
stand for every article in the archive, not for each year equally."""

from eval_a import draw, ocr_quality, summarise_composition, uniform

WORDS = frozenset(
    {"the", "ghost", "seen", "every", "night", "family", "report", "walk", "house"}
)


def test_ocr_quality_is_the_share_of_words_the_dictionary_knows():
    text = "The ghost was seen every night; the family re-\nport it walked the houses. Xqzt vvrm."
    # 14 words of three letters or more, and 11 are known once -ed and -s come off
    assert ocr_quality(text, WORDS, least=10) == 11 / 14
    assert ocr_quality("Too short to say.", WORDS) is None


def test_a_recall_sample_weights_each_year_by_its_share_of_the_pool():
    pools = {1800: list(range(100)), 1900: list(range(100)), 1950: list(range(100))}
    sizes = {1800: 1_000, 1900: 99_000, 1950: 0}

    picked = draw(pools, sizes, 50, seed="test")

    years = [year for year, _ in picked]
    assert len(set(picked)) == 50 and 1950 not in years and years.count(1900) > 40
    assert draw(pools, sizes, 50, seed="test") == picked


def test_a_uniform_pick_gives_every_candidate_the_same_chance():
    counts = {1800: 3, 1801: 0, 1802: 5}
    assert sorted(uniform(counts, 8, seed="x")) == [
        (1800, 0),
        (1800, 1),
        (1800, 2),
        (1802, 0),
        (1802, 1),
        (1802, 2),
        (1802, 3),
        (1802, 4),
    ]


def test_a_story_printed_in_several_papers_counts_once():
    picked = [
        {"category": "ghost_report", "printings": 2},
        {"category": "ghost_report", "printings": 1},
        {"category": "other", "printings": 1},
        {"category": "other", "printings": 4},
    ]
    ghosts = summarise_composition(picked, 400)["categories"]["ghost_report"]
    # each candidate is 1/k of a story when its cluster holds k printings
    assert (ghosts["implied"], ghosts["stories"]) == (200, 150)
