# Storage budget: Atlas M0

Measured on 2026-10-30 by `scripts/budget_probe.py`, which writes `eval/results/phase2b/budget.json`. Every number here comes from that file or follows from it by arithmetic. The documents are the final 2B.1 models (decision 33). Atlas M0 is the free tier, so nothing here costs money.

## What Atlas counts against the cap

- **The cap:** M0's storage is 0.5 GB, a hard limit. The cluster comparison writes it as "Storage (Data Size + Index Size) 512 MB". That is the documents' uncompressed BSON plus their B-tree indexes ([Free Cluster Limits](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/free-shared-limitations/), [Manage Clusters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-clusters/)).
- **How it's measured:** "Atlas calculates allocated storage using metrics returned by the dbStats command" ([FAQ: Storage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/faq/storage/)).
- **Search indexes:**
  - Atlas Search and Vector Search indexes aren't in `dbStats`.
  - Free clusters have no Search index size metrics ([Review Search Metrics](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-atlas-search-metrics/)).
  - So by the docs, Search indexes don't count against the cap. No page says so outright, though, and M0 can't measure them, so the budget leaves them out and keeps some headroom.
  - The cap of three Search indexes counts the whole cluster ([Search limitations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/limitations/)).
- **The figure used:** the budget plans against 500,000,000 bytes, the stricter of the two readings. Reading the cap as 512 MiB would add 36.9 MB.

## Free space now

| Database | Data | Indexes | Counted | On disk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sample_mflix` | 129.1 MB | 19.8 MB | **148.9 MB** | 239.2 MB |
| `paperghosts` | 0.003 MB | 0.6 MB | 0.6 MB | 11.3 MB |
| `cubby` (not this project's) | 0.0002 MB | 0.02 MB | 0.02 MB | 0.06 MB |

- **Free:** 350.5 MB with `sample_mflix`, and 499.4 MB without it.
- **`sample_mflix`:** its 239 MB on disk is compressed storage. Atlas counts 148.9 MB of it, its data plus its indexes.
- **`paperghosts`:** the 0.6 MB is the plan's empty indexes, which kept the pages the early probe runs used.

## Bytes per story

Two samples are built as full `reports` documents:
- **Text and printings:** real text, and every printing in the story's reprint cluster.
- **Embedding:** a float32 BinData vector.
- **Reader fields:** quotes that are real sentences of the article.

The samples:
- **The 1,000:** a seeded 1,000 of v2's candidates (seed "2B budget probe"). They make 1,000 stories with 5,116 printings. 29% have more than one printing, and the largest cluster has 487.
- **The judged reports:** the 24 of the 25 judged so far that v2 makes candidates.
  - These are eval A's 7, 3 of the screen's 4, and 2A.8's 14. The fourth of the screen's, the 1918 scout, isn't a v2 candidate, so it would never be stored.
  - They make 24 stories with 88 printings. 33% have more than one, and the most is 30.

| Part (mean bytes) | The 1,000 | Judged reports |
|---|---|---|
| text | 2,555 | 1,891 |
| headline and display headline | 102 | 125 |
| printings, apart from their boxes | 1,801 | 1,287 |
| printings' `bbox_list` | 502 | 395 |
| reader fields | 1,335 | 1,330 |
| embedding (float32) | 1,554 | 1,554 |
| the rest: ids, dates, place, versions, terms | 637 | 648 |
| **whole document** | **8,486** (median 6,995) | **7,230** (median 6,579) |

- **The reports are shorter than candidates in general,** with 1,891 bytes of text against 2,555, and reprinted about as often.
- **The budget takes each figure from whichever sample has more:**
  - a story's own bytes, without its printings, from the 1,000: 6,199
  - each printing's bytes from the reports: 454
- **Atlas's own sizes:** the 1,000 were loaded 500 at a time into a scratch collection with the reports validator and indexes, and it was dropped afterwards.
  - Data size is exactly the BSON bytes: 8,486,116.
  - The B-tree indexes take 401 bytes per story at 1,000, and 508 per story between 500 and 1,000. The budget uses 508.

    return np.array(sorted({i for a, b in spans for i in range(a, b)}), dtype=np.uint64)

input.content:
# Labelling reprint pairs (decision 36)

Each pair is two printings from American newspapers, 1770 to 1963, as AmericanStories' OCR gives them, often garbled. For each pair, decide whether the two are **one story**. You see each printing's paper, date, headline, and its first 400 words.

## same: one story

One printing is the other's text, printed again. Allow for all of these:
- OCR errors: misread letters and words, broken lines, stray characters
- cuts: one is shorter because paragraphs were dropped, or it stops early
- a new, missing or different headline
- a credit line, such as "From the Hartford Courant"
- paragraphs added or dropped at either end, such as a local introduction

An advertisement or notice printed again word for word is one story too.

## different: not one story

The two only share something smaller than a story:
- boilerplate: stock phrases, an advertisement's standard wording, a legal form, a masthead
- a quoted passage: the same verse, poem or quotation inside otherwise different articles
- different instalments of a serial: the same title, but different chapter text
- the same standing column or department with different content, such as "Local Brevities", or market reports of different days whose figures differ
- the same template with different particulars, such as testimonial advertisements quoting different people
- the same event told in different words, by different writers

Unrelated texts are different too.

## close: you can't decide

Use this when the text shown can't settle it. For example:
- it's too garbled or too short
- it's a borderline case, such as a table whose figures mostly agree

## What to write

For every pair, write its id, the label, and a note of fewer than 20 words. The note says what the two share or how they differ. A clear `same` may leave the note empty.

Judge only from the text shown. Don't guess from the papers or the dates.

"""The clustering evaluation's scoring: precision over the labelled pairs the stories keep
together, recall over the pairs labelled one story, and a cluster's least similar pair."""

import numpy as np

from clusters import least_similar, scored


def runs(a, b):
    return np.arange(a, b, dtype=np.uint64)


def test_precision_counts_the_pairs_kept_together_and_recall_those_labelled_one_story():
    index = {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 2, "d": 3}
    story = [0, 0, 2, 2]
    labelled = [
        {"pair": "kept and one story", "a": "a", "b": "b", "label": "same"},
        {"pair": "kept but two", "a": "c", "b": "d", "label": "different"},
        {"pair": "split but one", "a": "a", "b": "c", "label": "same"},
        {"pair": "split and two", "a": "b", "b": "d", "label": "different"},
    ]

    found = scored(index, story, labelled)

    assert (found["precision"]["hits"], found["precision"]["n"]) == (1, 2)
    assert (found["recall"]["hits"], found["recall"]["n"]) == (1, 2)
    assert found["false_merges"] == ["kept but two"]
    assert found["false_splits"] == ["split but one"]


def test_a_clusters_least_similar_pair_shares_least_of_the_shorters_shingles():
    found = {"shingles": {0: runs(0, 10), 1: runs(0, 9), 2: runs(5, 15)}}

    # 0 and 1 share all of 1's, 0 and 2 half of theirs, and 1 and 2 four of 1's nine
    assert least_similar(found, [0, 1, 2]) == (1, 2)

input.content:
**36. Reprint clusters become stories: eval A's links stay, but a printing joins a story only by matching the story's first printing directly, so no chain joins stories that share nothing. [results in the title once measured]**
- **What makes two printings one story:** one is the other's text printed again.
  - It allows OCR errors, cuts, a new or missing headline, a credit line, and paragraphs added or dropped at either end.
  - An advertisement or notice printed again word for word is one story too.
- **What doesn't:**
  - shared boilerplate: stock phrases, an advertisement's standard wording, a legal form, a masthead
  - a quoted passage: a verse, a poem or a quotation inside otherwise different articles
  - a serial's other instalments
  - a standing column or department with other content
  - a template with other particulars, such as testimonials quoting different people
  - the same event told in different words
  - `eval/clusters/LABELLING.md` is the reading agents' version.
- **Eval A's clusters (decision 27) and what changes:**
  - Eval A joins two candidates when they share a pair among their six smallest sampled seven-word runs, from their first 120 words. A pair held by more than 1,000 candidates is boilerplate.
  - It joins every linked pair, so a chain of links joins stories that share nothing. That gives v2's 91,301 clusters holding 30.3% of candidates, and its 952,591 distinct stories.
  - The links stay as they are, as the blocking. A pair of candidates the links don't join can't be one story, so a new cluster always sits inside one of eval A's. That's what lets an evaluation set drawn from eval A's clusters, before any tuning, cover every link the new method can make.
- **The stories** (`paperghosts/cluster/reprints.py`, `stories`):
  1. The printings are taken earliest first, ties by article id.
  2. Each looks at the stories of the printings it's linked to.
  3. It joins the one whose first printing it matches best, provided at least the threshold of the shorter's shingles are the other's. Otherwise it starts a story of its own.
  - Every member matches its story's first printing directly, so nothing chains.
  - **The shingles** (`shingles`): five-word runs of 3+ letters in the first 600 words, one in four kept by its own hash. They're shorter than the links' seven-word runs, so they weather OCR errors better, and they cover five times as much of the text.
  - The share is taken of the shorter printing, so a cut reprint is held whole in its original.
- **Stable ids:** a story's id is its first printing's article id. The same candidates give the same stories and the same ids on every run, which 2C's split by cluster needs.
- **The cost of a false merge:** if the reader reads one printing per story, a report merged into another story is never read.
  - So the threshold is chosen with a false merge costing five false splits.
  - **The reader also reads every member at least 25% longer than its story's first printing**, since the extra text might hold another story. A first version counted members with less than 80% of their shingles in the first printing. That flagged OCR noise, not added text: 166,717 members, against 19,416 by length.

**36. Reprint clusters become stories. Eval A's links stay, but a printing joins a story only by matching the story's first printing directly. That ends the chaining that joined different stories in 54 of the 207 largest clusters. Precision per candidate is 100% (97.7–100%), against eval A's 98.0%, and recall is 84.7%.**
- **What makes two printings one story:** one is the other's text printed again.
  - That allows OCR errors, cuts, a new or missing headline, a credit line, and paragraphs added or dropped at either end.
  - An advertisement or notice printed again word for word is one story too.
  - A printing held whole in a longer one is one story with it, so a notice and the column that holds it are one story.
- **What doesn't:**
  - shared boilerplate: stock phrases, an advertisement's standard wording, a legal form, a masthead
  - a quoted passage: a verse, a poem or a quotation inside otherwise different articles
  - a serial's other instalments
  - a standing column or department with other content
  - a template with other particulars, such as testimonials quoting different people
  - the same event told in different words
  - two fragments of one long text that hardly overlap, since neither printing holds the other. Merging them would leave the reader one fragment.
  - `eval/clusters/LABELLING.md` is the reading agents' version.
- **Eval A's clusters (decision 27), and what changes:**
  - Eval A joins two candidates that share a pair among their six smallest sampled seven-word runs, from their first 120 words. A pair held by more than 1,000 candidates is boilerplate.
  - It joins every linked pair, so a chain of links joins stories that share nothing. That gave v2's 91,301 clusters holding 30.3% of candidates, and 952,591 distinct stories.
  - The links stay as they are, as the blocking. The new method never joins candidates the links leave apart, so every story sits inside one of eval A's clusters. That's why an evaluation set drawn from eval A's clusters before any tuning covers every link the method can make.
- **The stories** (`paperghosts/cluster/reprints.py`, `stories`; `scripts/clusters.py`):
  1. The printings are taken earliest first, ties by article id.
  2. Each looks at the stories of the printings it is linked to.
  3. It joins the one whose first printing it matches best, where at least the threshold of the shorter's shingles are the other's. Otherwise it starts a story of its own.
  - Every member matches its story's first printing directly, so nothing chains.
  - **Shingles** (`shingles`) are five-word runs of 3+ letters in the first 600 words, one in four kept by its own hash. They are shorter than the links' seven-word runs, so they weather OCR errors better, and they cover five times as much of the text. The share is taken of the shorter printing, so a cut reprint is held whole in its original.
  - **The threshold is 0.25**, tuned on the dev set alone (`tune`, `eval/clusters/tuning.json`), with a false merge costing five false splits:

    | Threshold | 0.2 | 0.25 | 0.3 | 0.4 | 0.5 | 0.6 | 0.8 |

- **Article:** one article region from AmericanStories, with its text, headline, bounding boxes and page.

class Stated(Model):
    """One field the reader reads: its value, the verbatim quote it rests on, whether the
    verifier found that quote in the text, and the reader's score. A field with no verified
    quote is "not stated" and has no value."""

    # the same rule for Atlas's validator: no value, or a value with a verified quote
    model_config = ConfigDict(
        json_schema_extra={
            "anyOf": [

                {"required": ["quote"], "properties": {"verified": {"enum": [True]}}},
            ]
        }
    )

    value: str | None = None
    quote: str | None = None
    verified: bool
    score: Score

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def quoted(self) -> Self:
        if self.value is not None and not (self.quote and self.verified):
            raise ValueError("a stated value needs a quote that verified")
        return self

    people: list[Stated]
    seen: Stated
    outcome: StatedOutcome
    specific_place: Stated | None = None
    place_type: StatedPlaceType | None = None
    precision: StatedPrecision | None = None


class Report(Model):
    """One story: its printings, the text of its primary printing as printed, the reader's
    fields, where it happened and its embedding."""

    id: str = Field(alias="_id")
    primary_article_id: str
    printings: list[Printing] = Field(min_length=1)
    headline: str
    text: str
    display_headline: str
    date: IsoDate  # the earliest printing's
    year: Year
    month_day: Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^\d{2}-\d{2}$")]

    fields: Fields

    location_source: str | None = None
    place_id: Annotated[int, Field(ge=1)] | None = None
    town: str | None = None

    embedding: Vector | None = None
    versions: Versions
    lexicon_terms: list[LexiconTerm] = Field(min_length=1)
    case_id: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def ids(self) -> Self:
        if self.id != f"r_{self.primary_article_id}":
            raise ValueError("a report's _id is r_ and its primary article ID")
        if self.case_id is not None and self.case_id != f"c_{self.id}":

        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def dated(self) -> Self:

            year,
            month_day,
            year // 10 * 10,
        ):
            raise ValueError("a report's year, month_day and decade are its date's")
        return self

# Gold labelling policy (RDR-3)

These are the rules the gold set and the dev set are labelled by. This file was written and committed before the draw and before any label (decision 37). Every check of the reader rests on it.

Each rule names an example by article id, from items eval A and lexicon v2 judged (decisions 27, 30 and 31). The draw leaves out those articles and their groups. An example's label here is this policy's, which can differ from the earlier judgment: rule 2 changes one.

## What is labelled

One article as AmericanStories gives it: its headline, its OCR text, and the scan's crop where the OCR is unclear.
- Label what the article says, not what is likely true.
- Label before seeing any model's output.
- When a later decision changes a rule, the labels it touches are checked again, and the change is dated.

## kind

Each article gets exactly one kind:

| kind | What it is |
|---|---|
| `report` | A ghost, haunting, apparition, or spirit manifestation or communication, told as something that happened or was claimed to. It is tied to a particular occasion, place or person. |
| `fiction` | Stories, serials, poems, jokes, allegories and parodies, whatever their subject and however often reprinted. |
| `idiom` | A figure of speech: "give up the ghost", "not the ghost of a chance", haunt as a place frequented, "the spectre of war", "the ghost of the tariff". |
| `religious` | The Holy Ghost, sermons, hymns, prayers, Sunday-school lessons, saints, the Ghost Dance. |
| `advert` | An advertisement or a paid notice: patent medicines, theatre and illusion shows, books, real estate, and mediums' and clairvoyants' cards. |
| `other` | Everything else: names and titles, social events, OCR accidents, and essays or news about ghosts or spiritualism in general that tell no particular claim. |

## Rules for hard cases

1. **A ghost explained is still a report.** If the text gives a cause, the outcome is `explained`.
   - 1854: a voice taken for Phie's ghost is a trapped man, reached with a rope (`21_1854-11-16_p1_sn83021169_00514152792_1854111601_0398.json`): report, explained.
2. **Delusions and hallucinations, one rule.** A person's claim to have seen, heard or felt a ghost or spirit, on a particular occasion, is a report.
   - That holds whatever a court, a doctor or the paper makes of the person's mind.
   - Where the text calls the claim a delusion, a hallucination or insanity, the outcome is `explained`.
   - 1904: a defendant in court points at a spectre the paper calls imaginary (`6_1904-05-28_p1_sn84020358_00271744432_1904052801_1153.json`): report, explained.
   - 1909: a lunacy hearing, with spooks among a man's claims of persecution (`24_1909-08-31_p1_sn83025121_00294552327_1909083101_0987.json`): report, explained. **This overrules eval A's `other`.**
   - With no ghost or spirit claimed, a delusion is `other`. 1917: an insane man believes he is an aeroplane (`32_1917-11-02_pna_sn84024827_00211104776_1917110201_0388.json`).
3. **Spirit control, and a felt presence of the dead.** It is a report when a dead person's spirit is claimed, on a particular occasion, to have:
   - controlled someone
   - spoken or written through them
   - been felt present

   Examples:
   - 1895, Waterloo, Oregon: a man speaks under the control of Sitting Bull's spirit (`1_1895-05-24_pna_sn97071028_00416152664_1895052401_0955.json`).
   - 1898: a wife murderer's defence is that spirits controlled him (`8_1898-01-20_pNone_sn84029386_00295871477_1898012001_0669.json`).
   - 1918: a scout feels a touch on the shoulder with no one by, and takes it for the spirits of the unburied dead (`9_1918-04-21_p1_sn83030214_00206532257_1918042102_0461.json`).
   - A trance or hypnotism with no spirit claimed is `other`:
     - 1897, Alexandria: a trance prophecy (`16_1897-01-02_p7_sn84024442_211103073_1897010201_0249.json`)
     - 1902, Old Bridge: a hypnotized woman names a murderer (`21_1902-11-24_pna_sn84024441_100492052_1902112401_0152.json`)
     - 1888: Tennyson's waking trance (`40_1888-12-05_pna_sn90059522_00175033373_1888120501_0403.json`)
4. **Séance reports.** A séance told as having happened, with phenomena or messages claimed, is a report, whatever the writer thinks of them.
   - 1857, Middlebury: a spirit called Judd speaks through a trance medium (`17_1857-07-29_pna_sn83025667_00280777808_1857072901_0724.json`).
   - 1875, Chittenden: fourteen spirits materialize at the Eddys' (`4_1875-03-29_pna_sn84022473_00280777559_1875032901_0300.json`).
   - 1898, Sacramento: John Slater's test séance (`4_1898-01-12_pna_sn82015104_00280768790_1898011201_0105.json`).
   - A séance announced for later, or spiritualists in the news with no phenomenon told, is `other`.
     - 1890: spiritualists arrested in Chicago for obtaining money under false pretences (`7_1890-02-21_pna_sn91068075_00296022883_1890022101_0179.json`).
     - A French *séance* that is only a sitting of a body is `other`: 1890 (`26_1890-03-08_p1_sn88064492_00295874727_1890030802_0087.json`).
5. **A first-person claim of communication with a named dead person** is a report, even when it's made in a lecture, an interview or a letter with no particular sitting described. This confirms decision 31's call.
   - 1922: Conan Doyle says he has many times spoken with his dead son at séances (`12_1922-04-14_p2_sn85042243_00212478854_1922041401_0708.json`).
   - 1923: Rev. G. Vale Owen lectures on his communications with his dead father, mother and daughter (`4_1923-02-02_p21_sn83045462_00280657256_1923020201_0533.json`).
   - 1919: Mrs. Curran says the spirit Patience speaks through her (`11_1919-11-15_p22_sn83030214_00206532452_1919111501_0468.json`).
6. **A claim inside a doubtful narrative, and a claim inside a general essay.**
   - **A narrative printed as fact** is a report when it tells a particular claim, even if its truth is doubtful. The outcome is `unknown` unless the text says more.
     - 1857: in the Picaud ("real Monte Cristo") narrative, printed as true, the dying Allut says he has seen and spoken with a soul separated from its body (`1_1857-04-02_p1_sn83025802_00295862026_1857040201_0270.json`): report.
     - Told as a tale, with a title, a narrator and literary framing, the same matter is `fiction` (rule 9).
   - **An essay, letter, sermon or editorial** is a report when it tells a particular claim: a named person, an occasion.
     - 1907, Winnemucca: an editorial reports the claim that the dead Professor Hodgson has communicated, as he promised (`3_1907-02-23_p1_sn86076224_00332890414_1907022301_0155.json`): report.
   - **One about ghosts or spiritualism in general, with no particular claim,** is `other`:
     - 1858: a letter sorting mediums' phenomena into tricks and marvels (`11_1858-11-25_p3_sn83030213_00206530601_1858112501_0379.json`)

## Fields, for reports only

- **Every value carries a quote:** the shortest exact span of the OCR text that states it, copied as it is, OCR errors and all.
- **A value the text doesn't state is left empty,** which means "not stated". It is never inferred.

| Field | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `place` | Where the experience happened, as the text names it: "the old Hale farmhouse at Milford". |
| `place_state` | The state of that place, from the text or from its dateline. Gold uses it to measure the story-place rule, and the reader isn't asked for it. |
| `people` | Each person who saw, heard, felt or claimed it, by name if the text names them, or as the text describes them ("the family", "two boys"). At a séance, the medium and the sitters the text names are people. |
| `seen` | What was seen, heard or felt, as the text says it: "knockings upon the walls". |
| `outcome` | One of four values, set out below. |
| `specific_place` | For walks: the building, house, road or spot, if the text names one. |
| `place_type` | For walks: `house`, `church`, `cemetery`, `inn or hotel`, `road or bridge`, `public building`, `ship` or `other`. |
| `precision` | For walks: `town` if only a town is given, `street` for a street or road, `building` for a particular building or spot. |

**The four outcomes:**
- `explained`: the text gives a natural cause, such as a trapped man, rats, a reflection or a delusion.
- `hoax`: the text says someone deliberately deceived, such as fraud exposed or a prankster caught.
- `unexplained`: the text says no cause was found, or that it remains a mystery after a search.
- `unknown`: the text tells the claim and no more. Its quote is the sentence the account ends on.

**The story-place rule:**
- A town alone takes its state from the text: a county or state the text gives, or the dateline.
- Otherwise `place_state` stays empty.
- It is never taken from the paper's place or state. That guess put 2 of decision 34's 9 town-only places wrong.

## The label record

Labels are saved one JSON object per article, in `eval/gold/labels.jsonl` and `eval/gold/dev_labels.jsonl`, with these keys:
- `article_id`, `kind`, and `kind_quote` (the span that shows the kind)
- `place`, `place_state`, `seen`, `outcome`, `specific_place`, `place_type` and `precision`, each `{"value": …, "quote": …}` or `null`
- `people`, a list of `{"value": …, "quote": …}`
- `rules`: the numbers of the rules above that were applied
- `crop_used`: whether the crop was needed
- `note`, `labeller` and `labelled_at`

  - the `PlaceType` literals

- The rules:

  2. Delusions and hallucinations, one rule: a claim on an occasion is a report, and where the text says delusion the outcome is `explained`. It covers the 1904 spectre and the 1909 lunacy hearing, overruling eval A's `other`. A delusion with no ghost claimed is `other` (1917, the aeroplane).

  5. A first-person claim of communication with a named dead person counts: Conan Doyle, Vale Owen, Curran.

  9. Reprinted fiction is `fiction`.

```python
WORDS_SHOWN = 400  # of each printing, for the reading agents
# words past WORDS_SHOWN that both printings need before the unseen check compares their tails
TAIL = 50

def runs_of(text: str) -> set:
    """Every five-word run of 3+ letters in the text, none sampled."""
    words = WORD.findall(text.lower())
    return {" ".join(words[i : i + SHINGLE]) for i in range(len(words) - SHINGLE + 1)}

def overlap_of(a: set, b: set):
    """The share of the smaller set of runs the other holds."""
    return round(len(a & b) / min(len(a), len(b)), 4) if a and b else None

def unseen(found: dict, root: Path = ROOT) -> dict:
    # joined pairs (stories at THRESHOLD) in the per candidate / per cluster / near the threshold
    # strata; texts split on whitespace; a pair is counted if a printing is longer than 400 words;

def shingles(text, window=WINDOW, sample=SAMPLE):
    """... The leakage check reads every run of the whole text: window=None, sample=1."""
    text = (text or "") if window is None else (text or "")[:40000]
    words = WORD.findall(text.replace("-\n", "").lower())[:window]
    found = set()
    for i in range(len(words) - SHINGLE + 1):
        run = " ".join(words[i : i + SHINGLE]).encode()
        low = zlib.crc32(run)
        if low % sample == 0:
            found.add(zlib.crc32(run, 0x5BD1E995) << 32 | low)
    return np.array(sorted(found), dtype=np.uint64)
```

FEATURES = DATA / "features.pkl"

SETS = ROOT / "eval" / "clusters"
REPORT = ROOT / "eval" / "results" / "phase2b" / "clusters.json"

LARGE = 50  # printings in a cluster that gets its least similar pair checked by hand

# words past WORDS_SHOWN that both printings need before the unseen check compares their tails
TAIL = 50
EMPTY = np.array([], dtype=np.uint64)


def read_year(path: Path) -> list:
    """One year's candidates: id, date, LCCN, length in words of 3+ letters, the opening's
    runs, the body's runs (from word 120), and the shingles."""
    found = []
    with zstandard.open(path, "rt") as rows:
        for row in map(json.loads, rows):
            text = row["text"] or ""
            found.append(
                (
                    row["article_id"],
                    row["date"],
                    row["lccn"],
                    len(WORD.findall(text.lower())),
                    tuple(sorted(keys(text))),
                    tuple(sorted(keys(text, start=120))),
                    shingles(text),
                )
            )
    return found


def features(root: Path = ROOT) -> dict:
    """Every candidate's id, date, LCCN, runs and body runs; the shingles of those eval A
    clusters; and eval A's clusters themselves. Cached, since reading takes minutes."""
    if FEATURES.exists():
        return pickle.loads(FEATURES.read_bytes())
    paths = sorted((root / "data" / "candidates").glob("*.jsonl.zst"))
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
        rows = [row for year in pool.map(read_year, paths) for row in year]
    groups = clusters([set(r[4]) for r in rows], least=2)
    clustered = {d for g in groups for d in g}
    found = {
        "ids": [r[0] for r in rows],
        "dates": [r[1] for r in rows],
        "lccns": [r[2] for r in rows],
        "words": [r[3] for r in rows],
        "keys": [r[4] for r in rows],
        "body": [r[5] for r in rows],
        "shingles": {d: rows[d][6] for d in clustered},
        "frame": groups,
    }
    DATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    FEATURES.write_bytes(pickle.dumps(found, protocol=5))
    return found


def order_of(found: dict) -> list:
    """Every candidate, earliest first; a story's first printing names it."""
    return sorted(
        range(len(found["ids"])), key=lambda d: (found["dates"][d], found["ids"][d])
    )


def stories_at(found: dict, threshold: float) -> tuple:
    texts = [found["shingles"].get(d, EMPTY) for d in range(len(found["ids"]))]
    return stories(
        [set(k) for k in found["keys"]], texts, order_of(found), threshold, BOILERPLATE
    )


def similarity(found: dict, a: int, b: int) -> list:
    shared, of_shorter, of_longer = overlap(found["shingles"][a], found["shingles"][b])
    return [shared, round(of_shorter, 4), round(of_longer, 4)]


def least_similar(found: dict, group: list) -> tuple:
    """The pair of a cluster's printings that share the least of the shorter's shingles."""
    worst, pair = 2.0, (group[0], group[1])
    for i, a in enumerate(group):

            score = overlap(found["shingles"][a], found["shingles"][b])[1]
            if score < worst:
                worst, pair = score, (a, b)
    return pair


def report(found: dict, story: list, match: list, threshold: float) -> dict:
    """What the stories at threshold make of the candidates, beside eval A's clusters."""
    members = defaultdict(list)
    for doc, first in enumerate(story):
        members[first].append(doc)

import json, re, sys
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
import zstandard
from paperghosts.ingest.lexicon import ghost_terms
ORDER = ("ouija", "seance", "spirit_phrase", "spiritualism", "spirit+medium")
SHIP = re.compile(r"\b(?:phantom|ghost|spectre|specter|spectral)[\s-]+(?:ship|vessel|schooner|steamer|bark|brig|train|engine|light|lights|lantern)s?\b", re.I)
HOAX = re.compile(r"\bhoax|\bpractical jok|\bprankster", re.I)
FOREIGN = re.compile(r"\b(?:und|der|die|das|nicht|ein|ist|les|est|une|dans|pour|los|las|del|por|que|het|een|og|och)\b")
ENGLISH = re.compile(r"\b(?:the|and|of|to|was|that)\b")
def year(path):
    out = Counter()
    with zstandard.open(path, "rt") as rows:
        for row in map(json.loads, rows):
            terms = row["terms"]
            cls = next((t for t in ORDER if t in terms), "v1")
            head = bool(ghost_terms(row["headline"] or ""))
            dec = int(row["date"][:4]) // 10 * 10
            text = row["text"] or ""
            low = text.lower()
            f, e = len(FOREIGN.findall(low)), len(ENGLISH.findall(low))
            edge = ("E8" if SHIP.search(text) else "E12" if f >= 8 and f > 2 * e else "E6" if HOAX.search(text) else None)
            out[("class", cls, head)] += 1
            out[("decade", dec)] += 1
            out[("edge", edge)] += 1
            if edge: out[("edge-head", edge, head)] += 1
    return out
if __name__ == "__main__":
    paths = sorted(Path(sys.argv[1], "data", "candidates").glob("*.jsonl.zst"))
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
        total = sum(pool.map(year, paths), Counter())
    for k in sorted(total, key=str):
        if k[0] != "decade": print(k, total[k])
    print({k[1]: v for k, v in sorted(total.items(), key=str) if k[0] == "decade"})
EOF

## 7. Evaluation specifications
Results are saved as JSON plus a chart under `eval/results/`, and each is produced by one command.

### 7.1 Evals A to D
- **A, the archive read:**
  - pages and articles read, and candidates per year
  - reports per million articles, by year and by state
  - the term mix and an OCR-quality distribution
  - prefilter recall: a random-sample upper bound (rule of three when no misses are found) and the misses found in the near-miss pool, with the lexicon changes they caused
- **B, the reader:**
  - kind accuracy and macro-F1, and report precision, recall and F1
  - field match rates, and the share of quotes verified
  - the hallucinated-quote rate
  - cost per 10,000 articles and latency
  - bootstrap 95% intervals throughout
  - the headline is the accuracy gap and the cost per 10,000 articles
- **C, the investigations:** case files written, named deaths found, cases explained or exposed, then-and-now differences, the claim-verification rate and dropped claims, and Gemma against Ultramarine on the same cases (claims, verification rate, cost, latency).
- **D, the app:** Lighthouse on mobile, axe, contrast, e2e on phone and desktop in both modes, and the walks counts if walks are built.

### 7.2 Reader ablations
| ID | What changes | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | Base 4B, tuned 4B, teacher | The headline comparison |
| B2 | Training set size (a learning curve of at least 3 points) | Whether more teacher labels would help |
| B3 | LoRA rank and learning rate (a small grid, within credits) | Picks the trained model |
| B4 | Output format: fields with quotes against kind only | The cost of grounding |
| B5 | Quote verifier on and off, plus a threshold sweep | Precision of the fields shown |
| B6 | Triage on and off | Reports lost against cost saved |
| B7 | Slices by OCR quality | Robustness to rough scans |
| B8 | Slices by decade | Language drift from 1774 to 1963 |
| B9 | Base 4B zero-shot against few-shot | Makes the baseline fair |
| B10 | Reprint leakage removed, or not | Proves the scores aren't inflated |

Model selection uses a dev split. The gold set is used only for these final runs.

| ING-5 | Each year writes a random non-candidate sample and a near-miss pool. | Files exist, and eval A has a recall section |
| ING-6 | The crop builder handles single-column and multi-column articles (`bbox_list`). It is checked on 50 random candidates spread across as many batches as the sample allows. | `eval/results/crop_check.json`, plus a contact sheet image |

### 2.2 Reader (RDR)
| ID | Requirement | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| RDR-1 | The gold set has 150–300 articles, stratified by decade and term. It is frozen and hashed before training, and the split is committed. | `eval/gold/split.json` and `eval/gold/HASH`, unchanged in git history after the freeze |
| RDR-2 | The label schema covers: `kind` (report, fiction, idiom, religious, advert, other); place, people, seen and outcome (unexplained, explained, hoax, unknown); and, for walks, specific place, place type (house, church, cemetery, inn or hotel, road or bridge, public building, ship, other) and precision. Each value carries a verbatim quote. | Schema tests |
| RDR-3 | `eval/gold/POLICY.md` holds the rules for hard cases and is written before any labelling. | Git history order |
| RDR-4 | Training data is disjoint from the gold set, including reprints of gold stories. | `scripts/check_leakage.py` exits 0 |
| RDR-5 | LoRA training runs on Tinker. The configs, checkpoints and seeds are recorded. | `eval/results/reader_runs.json` |
| RDR-6 | Eval B compares base 4B, tuned 4B and the teacher on the gold set. It reports metrics with bootstrap 95% intervals, cost per 10,000 articles, and p50 and p95 latency. | `eval/results/reader_eval.json`, plus charts |
| RDR-7 | Every ablation in section 7.2 is run, or its absence is explained. | Ablation JSON and charts |
| RDR-8 | The edge-case suite in section 7.3 is reported slice by slice. | `eval/results/reader_edge_cases.json` |
| RDR-9 | The quote verifier's threshold is calibrated on the gold set. A field whose quote doesn't verify becomes "not stated". | Calibration curve, plus unit tests |
| RDR-10 | The tuned student runs locally with no network, on at least 200 articles, and its agreement with the Tinker-served outputs is reported. A guard in the runner blocks sockets, so system network settings are never touched. | `scripts/offline_proof.py` output |

"""Printings of one story share runs of words, give or take OCR errors and an extra line at
the start. An unrelated article doesn't join them, nor does stock phrasing that too many
articles share, nor one quoted run on its own. And a printing joins a story only by matching
its first printing directly, never through a chain of links (decision 36)."""

import numpy as np

from paperghosts.cluster.reprints import clusters, keys, overlap, shingles, stories

STORY = (
    "A strange story comes from the village of Milford, where the family of Mr. John Hale "
    "have been disturbed every night for a fortnight by knockings upon the walls of the old "
    "farmhouse which no search has been able to explain. The neighbors who have sat up with "
    "the family declare that they heard the sounds plainly and saw nothing at all, and the "
    "minister who visited the house on Sunday says he cannot account for the noises, though "
    "he does not believe that spirits have anything to do with them."
)
# the same story in another paper: a credit line first, and a few words misread
REPRINT = "From the Hartford Courant.\n" + STORY.replace(
    "farmhouse", "farmhonse"
).replace("fortnight", "fortuight")
OTHER = (
    "The county commissioners met on Tuesday and voted to repair the bridge over Mill creek "
    "before the spring freshets, the contract going to the lowest bidder. The treasurer "
    "reported that the taxes for the year have been nearly all collected, and that the county "
    "will close the year with a balance in the treasury for the first time since the war."
)


def test_printings_of_one_story_cluster_and_others_stay_apart():
    assert keys(STORY) and keys(STORY) & keys(REPRINT)

def shingles(text, window=WINDOW, sample=SAMPLE):
    """What two printings are compared on: hashes of the five-word runs in the article's first
    600 words of 3+ letters, one in four kept by its own hash as keys does, as a sorted array.
    Shorter runs than keys' seven weather OCR errors better. The leakage check reads every run
    of the whole text: window=None, sample=1."""
    text = (text or "") if window is None else (text or "")[:40000]
    words = WORD.findall(text.replace("-\n", "").lower())[:window]
    found = set()
    for i in range(len(words) - SHINGLE + 1):
        run = " ".join(words[i : i + SHINGLE]).encode()
        low = zlib.crc32(run)
        if low % sample == 0:
            found.add(zlib.crc32(run, 0x5BD1E995) << 32 | low)
    return np.array(sorted(found), dtype=np.uint64)


def overlap(a, b):
    """How much two printings share: the shingles they share, and those as a share of the
    shorter's shingles and of the longer's. A cut reprint is held whole in its original, which
    it holds only part of."""
    if not len(a) or not len(b):
        return 0, 0.0, 0.0
    shared = len(np.intersect1d(a, b, assume_unique=True))
    return shared, shared / min(len(a), len(b)), shared / max(len(a), len(b))


def stories(doc_keys, doc_shingles, order, threshold, boilerplate=BOILERPLATE):
    """Printings grouped into stories without chaining (decision 36). Each printing, earliest
    first (`order`), looks at the stories of the printings it shares a pair of runs with, as
    `clusters` links them. It joins the story whose first printing it matches best, where at
    least `threshold` of the shorter's shingles are the other's; otherwise it starts a story
    of its own. Returns each document's story, as the index of its first printing, and its
    match to that printing (1.0 for a first printing)."""
    assert len(doc_keys) < 1 << DOC_BITS
    mask = (1 << DOC_BITS) - 1
    entries = sorted(
        key << DOC_BITS | doc
        for doc, held in enumerate(doc_keys)
        for key in pairs(held)
    )
    links = [[] for _ in doc_keys]  # each document's shared pairs of runs, by number
    shared, start = 0, 0
    for end in range(1, len(entries) + 1):
        if (
            end < len(entries)
            and entries[end] >> DOC_BITS == entries[start] >> DOC_BITS
        ):
            continue
        if 2 <= end - start <= boilerplate:
            for entry in entries[start:end]:
                links[entry & mask].append(shared)
            shared += 1
        start = end
    rank = {doc: i for i, doc in enumerate(order)}
    seen = [
        [] for _ in range(shared)
    ]  # the stories of the printings seen with each pair
    story, match = list(range(len(doc_keys))), [1.0] * len(doc_keys)
    for doc in order:
        best, score = doc, 0.0
        heard = {first for pair in links[doc] for first in seen[pair]}
        for first in sorted(heard, key=rank.__getitem__):
            of_shorter = overlap(doc_shingles[doc], doc_shingles[first])[1]
            if of_shorter >= threshold and of_shorter > score:
                best, score = first, of_shorter
        story[doc] = best
        match[doc] = score if best != doc else 1.0
        for pair in links[doc]:
            if best not in seen[pair]:
                seen[pair].append(best)
    return story, match

"""RDR-4's check: a pool article that reprints a gold or dev article leaks, judged on whole
texts; a shared stock phrase or a quoted paragraph doesn't. A group of the inclusive grouping
that spans the split fails it."""

import json

import check_leakage
import zstandard
from check_leakage import between, crossings, flagged, leaks, runs

STORY = " ".join(
    f"word{chr(97 + i % 26)}{chr(97 + i // 26 % 26)}{chr(97 + i // 676)}"
    for i in range(300)
)
OTHER = " ".join(
    f"other{chr(97 + i % 26)}{chr(97 + i // 26 % 26)}{chr(97 + i // 676)}"
    for i in range(300)
)


def test_a_reprint_shares_enough_of_the_shorters_runs_and_a_quotation_doesnt():
    words = STORY.split()
    cut = " ".join(words[:60])  # the story cut short, as a reprint often is
    quoted = " ".join(OTHER.split()[:150] + words[100:115] + OTHER.split()[150:])

    assert len(runs(STORY)) == 296 and flagged(56, len(runs(cut)), 296)
    assert between({"story": STORY}, {"cut": cut, "other": OTHER}) == [("story", "cut")]
    # a quoted paragraph of 15 words: 11 runs, past FEWEST but under LEAK of the shorter
    assert between({"story": STORY}, {"quoted": quoted}) == []
    assert not flagged(4, 4, 296)  # a stock phrase or two: too few runs, however short


def test_the_pool_scan_finds_a_reprint_outside_the_excluded_and_skips_the_random_reservoir(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    rows = {
        "candidates": [
            {"article_id": "reprint", "text": "From the Courant. " + STORY},
            {"article_id": "unrelated", "text": OTHER},
            {"article_id": "gold's own group", "text": STORY},
        ],
        "samples": [
            {"article_id": "random one", "sample": "random", "text": STORY},
            {"article_id": "near miss", "sample": "near_miss", "text": STORY[:900]},
        ],
    }
    for folder, items in rows.items():
        (tmp_path / "data" / folder).mkdir(parents=True)
        with zstandard.open(tmp_path / "data" / folder / "1890.jsonl.zst", "wt") as f:
            f.writelines(json.dumps(item) + "\n" for item in items)
    monkeypatch.setattr(check_leakage, "ROOT", tmp_path)

    found = leaks(tmp_path, {"gold": STORY}, excluded={"gold's own group"}, workers=1)

    assert sorted((pool, held) for pool, held, *_ in found) == [
        ("near miss", "gold"),
        ("reprint", "gold"),
    ]


def test_a_group_that_holds_gold_and_the_pool_or_gold_and_dev_crosses_the_split():
    found = {
        "ids": ["g", "g's reprint", "d", "d's reprint", "q", "q's reprint", "free"],
        "group": ["g", "g", "d", "g", "q", "q", "free"],
    }

    # g's reprint is held out, but d sits in g's group, and q's reprint is still in the pool
    assert crossings(
        found, gold={"g"}, dev={"d"}, held={"g", "d", "q"}, out={"g's reprint", "d's reprint"}
    ) == ["g", "q"]
    assert (
        crossings(
            found,
            gold={"g"},
            dev=set(),
            held={"g", "q"},
            out={"g's reprint", "d", "d's reprint", "q's reprint"},
        )
        == []
    )

"""The gold set's draw and the split (decision 37), seeded, after POLICY.md and before any label.

Every candidate falls in one stratum, the first of these that fits:
1. three edge-case slices the archive holds too few of to meet by chance (SRS 7.3): phantom
   ships, trains and lights (E8), hoaxes and pranksters (E6), and text not in English (E12)
2. printed before 1850, so the early decades are read
3. otherwise the rarest of lexicon v2's five rules it holds, or none, split by whether a ghost
   term is in the headline. A term in the headline is where reports gather: 7 of 27 judged
   against 14 of 373.

A near-miss stratum comes from the near-miss reservoir, each year in proportion to its pool,
so triage can be measured on gold. Within a candidate stratum the draw is systematic in date
order, so each decade gets its share. Each article's inclusion probability is its stratum's
draw over its size. Dev is drawn the same way at half the size, from outside gold's groups.
POLICY.md's examples and their groups are left out of both.

The training pool is every other article of the candidates and the near-miss reservoir,
outside the groups of gold and dev, and outside the quarantine: the pool articles the
whole-text check finds reprinting a gold or dev article, with their groups. Writes
eval/gold/split.json, its sha256 in eval/gold/HASH, and the design's numbers in
eval/results/phase2c/gold_draw.json.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import random
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import zstandard
from check_leakage import (
    FEWEST,
    HASH,
    LEAK,
    RESULTS,
    SPLIT,
    between,
    examples,
    frame,
    leaks,
    whole_texts,
)
from eval_a import draw

from paperghosts.ingest.lexicon import ghost_terms
from paperghosts.stats import wilson

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SEED = "2C.1 gold"
RULES = ("ouija", "seance", "spirit_phrase", "spiritualism", "spirit+medium")  # rarest first
SHIPS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:phantom|ghost|spectre|specter|spectral)[\s-]+"
    r"(?:ship|vessel|schooner|steamer|bark|brig|train|engine|light|lantern)s?\b",
    re.I,
)
HOAX = re.compile(r"\bhoax|\bpractical jok|\bprankster", re.I)
# common short words of German, French, Spanish, Dutch and the Scandinavian languages
FOREIGN = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:und|der|die|das|nicht|ein|ist|les|est|une|dans|pour|los|las|del|por|que"
    r"|het|een|og|och)\b"
)
ENGLISH = re.compile(r"\b(?:the|and|of|to|was|that)\b")
NEAR = "near misses"
# (gold, dev) for each stratum, in the order a candidate is placed
ALLOCATION = {
    "E8: phantom ships, trains and lights": (8, 4),
    "E6: hoaxes and pranksters": (8, 4),
    "E12: not in English": (7, 3),
    "before 1850": (20, 10),
    "ouija, term in the headline": (8, 4),
    "ouija, none in the headline": (12, 6),
    "seance, term in the headline": (10, 5),
    "seance, none in the headline": (12, 6),
    "spirit_phrase, term in the headline": (10, 5),
    "spirit_phrase, none in the headline": (12, 6),
    "spiritualism, term in the headline": (10, 5),
    "spiritualism, none in the headline": (12, 6),
    "spirit+medium, term in the headline": (6, 3),
    "spirit+medium, none in the headline": (14, 7),
    "v1 terms only, term in the headline": (80, 40),
    "v1 terms only, none in the headline": (46, 23),
    NEAR: (25, 13),
}
JUDGED = ROOT / "eval" / "results"


def stratum(row: dict) -> str:
    text = row["text"] or ""
    if SHIPS.search(text):
        return "E8: phantom ships, trains and lights"
    if HOAX.search(text):
        return "E6: hoaxes and pranksters"
    low = text.lower()
    foreign = len(FOREIGN.findall(low))
    if foreign >= 8 and foreign > 2 * len(ENGLISH.findall(low)):
        return "E12: not in English"
    if row["date"] < "1850":
        return "before 1850"
    rule = next((t for t in RULES if t in row["terms"]), "v1 terms only")
    headline = "term in the headline" if ghost_terms(row["headline"] or "") else "none"
    return f"{rule}, {headline if headline != 'none' else 'none in the headline'}"


def strata_in(path: Path) -> list:
    with zstandard.open(path, "rt") as rows:
        return [(row["article_id"], stratum(row)) for row in map(json.loads, rows)]


def systematic(units: list, n: int, rng: random.Random) -> list:
    """n of the units, which are in date order: one every len(units) / n from a seeded start.
    Each is drawn with probability n / len(units), and each decade gets its share of the n,
    give or take one."""
    step = len(units) / n
    start = rng.random() * step
    return [units[min(int(start + i * step), len(units) - 1)] for i in range(n)]


def take(units: dict, near: dict, sizes: dict, banned: set, which: int, seed: str):
    """Each stratum's draw, for gold (which=0) or dev (which=1), from the articles outside
    `banned`, with the number of articles it was drawn from."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = {}
    for name, counts in ALLOCATION.items():
        if name == NEAR:
            pools = {y: [a for a in ids if a not in banned] for y, ids in near.items()}
            picks = draw(pools, sizes, counts[which], f"{seed} near misses")
            size = sum(sizes[y] for y, ids in pools.items() if ids and sizes.get(y))
            out[name] = ([aid for _, aid in picks], size)
        else:
            eligible = sorted(u for u in units[name] if u[1] not in banned)
            out[name] = (
                [aid for _, aid in systematic(eligible, counts[which], rng)],
                len(eligible),
            )
    return out


def items(drawn: dict, found: dict, index: dict) -> list:
    return [
        {
            "article_id": aid,
            "stratum": name,
            "date": found["dates"][index[aid]],
            "group": found["group"][index[aid]],
            "pi": len(ids) / size,
            "weight": size / len(ids),
        }
        for name, (ids, size) in drawn.items()
        for aid in ids
    ]


def members(found: dict, of: set) -> set:
    """Every article in the groups of these articles."""
    index = {aid: i for i, aid in enumerate(found["ids"])}
    wanted = {found["group"][index[aid]] for aid in of if aid in index}
    return {
        aid
        for aid, group in zip(found["ids"], found["group"], strict=True)
        if group in wanted
    }


def rate_class(name: str) -> str:
    """Where a stratum's report rate is read from: the five rules' strata pool their judged
    items, which are too few apart."""
    rule, _, headline = name.partition(", ")
    return f"a v2 rule, {headline}" if rule in RULES else name


def judged_rates(placed: dict) -> dict:
    """The report rate of each rate class, on what eval A and lexicon v2 judged (decisions 27,
    30 and 31): eval A's 200 candidates, lexicon v2's 200 added ones, and eval A's 300 from
    the near-miss reservoirs."""
    seen = [
        (x["article_id"], x["category"] == "ghost_report")
        for x in json.loads((JUDGED / "eval_a" / "composition.json").read_text())
    ] + [
        (x["article_id"], x["ghost_report"])
        for x in json.loads((JUDGED / "eval_a_v2" / "added.json").read_text())
    ]
    tally = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    for aid, report in seen:
        cell = tally[rate_class(placed[aid])]
        cell[0] += report
        cell[1] += 1
    for x in json.loads((JUDGED / "eval_a" / "recall.json").read_text()):
        if x["pool"] == "near_miss":
            tally[NEAR][0] += x["ghost_report"]
            tally[NEAR][1] += 1
    return dict(tally)


def expected(rates: dict, sizes: dict) -> dict:
    """Gold's expected reports, stratum by stratum, at the judged rates, with each Wilson
    interval's ends. The total's range adds those ends, so it is wider than its own interval."""
    rows, total = {}, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    for name, (n, _) in ALLOCATION.items():
        hits, judged = rates.get(rate_class(name), (0, 0))
        if not judged:
            rows[name] = {"gold": n, "judged": "none", "reports": None}
            continue
        low, high = wilson(hits, judged)
        row = [n * hits / judged, n * low, n * high]
        total = [t + r for t, r in zip(total, row, strict=True)]
        rows[name] = {
            "gold": n,
            "drawn_from": sizes[name],
            "judged": f"{hits} of {judged}",
            "reports": [round(r, 1) for r in row],
        }
    return {"strata": rows, "total": [round(t, 1) for t in total]}


def main(root: Path = ROOT) -> None:
    found = frame(root)
    index = {aid: i for i, aid in enumerate(found["ids"])}
    paths = sorted((root / "data" / "candidates").glob("*.jsonl.zst"))
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
        placed = dict(pair for year in pool.map(strata_in, paths) for pair in year)
    units = defaultdict(list)
    for aid, name in placed.items():
        units[name].append((found["dates"][index[aid]], aid))
    near = defaultdict(list)
    for aid in found["ids"][found["candidates"] :]:
        near[found["dates"][index[aid]][:4]].append(aid)
    sizes = {
        p.stem: json.loads(p.read_text())["near_miss"]
        for p in sorted((root / "data" / "counts").glob("*.json"))
    }

    named = examples(root)
    banned = named | members(found, named)
    gold = take(units, near, sizes, banned, 0, SEED)
    gold_ids = {aid for ids, _ in gold.values() for aid in ids}
    texts = whole_texts(root, gold_ids)
    dev_banned = banned | members(found, gold_ids)
    while True:  # a dev article reprinting a gold one is left out with its group, and redrawn
        dev = take(units, near, sizes, dev_banned, 1, f"{SEED} dev")
        dev_ids = {aid for ids, _ in dev.values() for aid in ids}
        texts |= whole_texts(root, dev_ids - texts.keys())
        clash = between(
            {a: texts[a] for a in gold_ids}, {a: texts[a] for a in dev_ids}
        )
        if not clash:
            break
        dev_banned |= members(found, {d for _, d in clash})
        print("redrawing dev without", clash)

    out = members(found, gold_ids | dev_ids)
    flagged = leaks(root, texts, out)
    quarantine = sorted({pool for pool, *_ in flagged})
    out |= set(quarantine) | members(found, set(quarantine))

    split = {
        "decision": 37,
        "seed": SEED,
        "policy_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
            (root / "eval" / "gold" / "POLICY.md").read_bytes()
        ).hexdigest(),
        "rule": {"leak": LEAK, "fewest": FEWEST},
        "strata": [
            {
                "stratum": name,
                "gold": len(gold[name][0]),
                "gold_drawn_from": gold[name][1],
                "dev": len(dev[name][0]),
                "dev_drawn_from": dev[name][1],
            }
            for name in ALLOCATION
        ],
        "gold": items(gold, found, index),
        "dev": items(dev, found, index),
        "quarantine": [
            {"article_id": pool, "reprints": held, "shared": n, "share": share}
            for pool, held, n, share in sorted(flagged)
        ],
        "out_of_pool": sorted(out),
        "pool": (
            "Every other article of the candidates and the near-miss reservoir. 2C.4 draws at "
            "most one printing per story from it."
        ),
    }
    SPLIT.write_text(json.dumps(split, indent=1) + "\n")
    HASH.write_text(f"{hashlib.sha256(SPLIT.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}  split.json\n")

    rates = judged_rates(placed)
    decade = lambda drawn: dict(  # noqa: E731
        sorted(
            Counter(
                found["dates"][index[a]][:3] + "0s"
                for ids, _ in drawn.values()
                for a in ids
            ).items()
        )
    )
    sizes_of = Counter(found["group"])
    report = {
        "population": dict(sorted(Counter(placed.values()).items())),
        "judged_rates": {k: f"{h} of {n}" for k, (h, n) in sorted(rates.items())},
        "expected_reports": expected(rates, {k: v[1] for k, v in gold.items()}),
        "decades": {"gold": decade(gold), "dev": decade(dev)},
        "grouping": {
            "articles": len(found["ids"]),
            "groups_of_two_or_more": sum(1 for s in sizes_of.values() if s > 1),
            "articles_in_them": sum(s for s in sizes_of.values() if s > 1),
            "largest": max(sizes_of.values()),
        },
        "split": {
            "gold": len(gold_ids),
            "dev": len(dev_ids),
            "left_out_for_policy_examples": len(banned),
            "quarantine": len(quarantine),
            "out_of_pool": len(out),
            "pool": len(found["ids"]) - len(out),
        },
    }
    RESULTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (RESULTS / "gold_draw.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps({k: report[k] for k in ("split", "grouping", "decades")}, indent=1))
    print("expected reports", report["expected_reports"]["total"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    """One crop per box, in the scan's own pixels at half size, in bbox_list's order, which

    return [

def get(url, **params):
    """A GET to the Library of Congress: at most one a second, or one in 3.5 s to loc.gov's
    JSON API, naming the project, and asked again after a pause while the server is busy:
    a 429, a 5xx or a CAPTCHA page. tile.loc.gov can answer a crop it hasn't made yet with a
    503. A CAPTCHA page still there after the pauses raises Busy, and is never cached."""
    return None


def batch(service: str) -> str:
    """The LoC batch that holds the page, from its IIIF service."""
    return re.search(r":batch_(\w+?):data:", service)[1]


def crop(url: str) -> Path:
    """The crop at url, from the cache, which is keyed by the URL, or fetched once into it."""
    path = CROPS / f"{hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).hexdigest()[:24]}.jpg"
    if not path.exists():
        response = get(url)
        if not response.headers.get("content-type", "").startswith("image/"):
            raise ValueError(f"tile.loc.gov sent no image for {url}")
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        partial = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial")
        partial.write_bytes(response.content)
        partial.replace(path)
    return path


def crops_for(
    member: str,
    scan: dict,
    boxes: list[dict],
    service: str | None = None,
    text: str | None = None,
):
    """The page's IIIF service and its crops, one per box.
    - A page whose member and batch path agree is shown unchecked. A batch path can name a
      batch that LoC has since reissued (ver01 where it now serves ver02), so when a crop
      from it is missing, loc.gov names the page's current service.
    - Any other page is checked against its article's text before any crop is fetched
      (page_check, decision 35): a page with no batch path, and one whose member names another
      frame or reel. A page with no batch path tries its reel's batches in turn. Where none of
      them holds the page, loc.gov names its batch, and that page is checked too."""
    raw = scan.get("raw_data_loc")
    if raw and agrees(member, raw):
        service = service or service_id(raw)
        try:
            return service, [crop(url) for url in crop_urls(service, boxes)]
        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
            if exc.response.status_code != 404:
                raise
        service = listed(*place(service))
        return service, [crop(url) for url in crop_urls(service, boxes)]
    page = MEMBER.search(member)
    trials = [service] if service else []
    if not trials:
        trials = [batch_path_service(member, raw)] if raw else mapped(member)
    reasons = []
    for trial in trials:
        why = page_check(trial, scan, boxes, text)
        if why is None:
            return trial, [crop(url) for url in crop_urls(trial, boxes)]
        reasons.append(why)
    held = [why for why in reasons if why != NO_SUCH_PAGE]

        raise LookupError(f"{member}: {held[0]}")

## Fields, for reports only

- **Every value carries a quote:** the shortest exact span of the OCR text that states it, copied as it is, OCR errors and all.
- **A value the text doesn't state is left empty,** which means "not stated". It is never inferred.

| Field | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `place` | Where the experience happened, as the text names it: "the old Hale farmhouse at Milford". |
| `place_state` | The state of that place, from the text or from its dateline. Gold uses it to measure the story-place rule, and the reader isn't asked for it. |
| `people` | Each person who saw, heard, felt or claimed it, by name if the text names them, or as the text describes them ("the family", "two boys"). At a séance, the medium and the sitters the text names are people. |
| `seen` | What was seen, heard or felt, as the text says it: "knockings upon the walls". |
| `outcome` | One of four values, set out below. |
| `specific_place` | For walks: the building, house, road or spot, if the text names one. |
| `place_type` | For walks: `house`, `church`, `cemetery`, `inn or hotel`, `road or bridge`, `public building`, `ship` or `other`. |
| `precision` | For walks: `town` if only a town is given, `street` for a street or road, `building` for a particular building or spot. |

**The four outcomes:**
- `explained`: the text gives a natural cause, such as a trapped man, rats, a reflection or a delusion.
- `hoax`: the text says someone deliberately deceived, such as fraud exposed or a prankster caught.
- `unexplained`: the text says no cause was found, or that it remains a mystery after a search.
- `unknown`: the text tells the claim and no more. Its quote is the sentence the account ends on.

**The story-place rule:**
- A town alone takes its state from the text: a county or state the text gives, or the dateline.
- Otherwise `place_state` stays empty.
- It is never taken from the paper's place or state. That guess put 2 of decision 34's 9 town-only places wrong.

## The label record

Labels are saved one JSON object per article, in `eval/gold/labels.jsonl` and `eval/gold/dev_labels.jsonl`, with these keys:
- `article_id`, `kind`, and `kind_quote` (the span that shows the kind)
- `place`, `place_state`, `seen`, `outcome`, `specific_place`, `place_type` and `precision`, each `{"value": …, "quote": …}` or `null`
- `people`, a list of `{"value": …, "quote": …}`
- `rules`: the numbers of the rules above that were applied
- `crop_used`: whether the crop was needed
- `note`, `labeller` and `labelled_at`

"""The labelling page serves an article's text beside its crops, with RDR-2's fields, and saves
a label only when every quote is in the text, one per article and labeller."""

import json

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from label_gold import app

TEXT = (
    "MILFORD, Conn., June 3.-The family of Mr. John Hale have been disturbed every night\n"
    "for a fortnight by knockings upon the walls of the old farmhouse, which no search has\n"
    "been able to explain."
)
ROW = {
    "article_id": "a1",
    "split": "gold",
    "paper": "The Courant",
    "date": "1890-06-05",
    "headline": "A HAUNTED FARMHOUSE",
    "text": TEXT,
    "member": "m",
    "scan": {"raw_data_loc": "r"},
    "bbox_list": [{"x0": 0, "y0": 0, "x1": 10, "y1": 10}],
}
CROP = "0123456789abcdef01234567.jpg"
REPORT = {
    "article_id": "a1",
    "kind": "report",
    "kind_quote": "disturbed every night for a fortnight by knockings",
    "place": {"value": "the old farmhouse", "quote": "the old farmhouse"},
    "place_state": {"value": "Connecticut", "quote": "MILFORD, Conn."},
    "seen": {"value": "knockings upon the walls", "quote": "knockings upon the walls"},
    "outcome": {"value": "unexplained", "quote": "which no search has\n been able to explain"},
    "people": [{"value": "the family of Mr. John Hale", "quote": "The family of Mr. John Hale"}],
    "rules": [1],
}


def client(tmp_path, asked):
    (tmp_path / CROP).write_bytes(b"\xff\xd8 a jpeg")

    def crops_for(member, scan, boxes, text=None):
        asked.append((member, len(boxes), text))
        return "service", [tmp_path / CROP]

    out = {"gold": tmp_path / "labels.jsonl", "dev": tmp_path / "dev_labels.jsonl"}
    return TestClient(app({"a1": ROW}, "tester", crops_for, out, tmp_path)), out


def test_it_serves_the_text_beside_its_crops_with_the_fields_and_the_rules(tmp_path):
    asked = []
    web, _ = client(tmp_path, asked)

    page = web.get("/article/a1")

    assert page.status_code == 200
    assert "knockings upon the walls" in page.text and f'src="/crop/{CROP}"' in page.text
    assert asked == [("m", 1, TEXT)]  # through crops_for, which checks the page first
    assert 'data-name="outcome"' in page.text and "inn or hotel" in page.text
    assert "Phantom ships, trains and lights" in page.text  # POLICY.md's rule 14, at hand
    assert web.get(f"/crop/{CROP}").content == b"\xff\xd8 a jpeg"
    assert web.get("/crop/..%2Flabels.jsonl").status_code == 404


def test_it_saves_a_label_whose_quotes_are_in_the_text_and_refuses_one_that_isnt(tmp_path):
    web, out = client(tmp_path, [])

    refused = web.post("/label", json={**REPORT, "seen": {"value": "a light", "quote": "a light"}})
    assert refused.status_code == 422 and "isn't in the text" in refused.json()["detail"]
    assert not out["gold"].exists()

    assert web.post("/label", json=REPORT).status_code == 200
    assert web.post("/label", json={**REPORT, "note": "checked twice"}).status_code == 200

    (saved,) = [json.loads(line) for line in out["gold"].read_text().splitlines()]
    assert saved["kind"] == "report" and saved["labeller"] == "tester"
    assert saved["outcome"]["value"] == "unexplained" and saved["note"] == "checked twice"
    assert saved["people"] == REPORT["people"] and saved["specific_place"] is None
    assert list(saved)[:3] == ["article_id", "kind", "kind_quote"]


def test_fields_are_for_reports_only_and_choices_come_from_the_schema(tmp_path):
    web, _ = client(tmp_path, [])

    idiom = {**REPORT, "kind": "idiom"}
    assert web.post("/label", json=idiom).json()["detail"] == "fields are for reports only"
    odd = {**REPORT, "outcome": {"value": "spooky", "quote": "the old farmhouse"}}
    assert "not one of" in web.post("/label", json=odd).json()["detail"]

On `phase-2c-reader`. I checked origin with `git ls-remote`: it shows `{HEAD}`, the same as local. There's no PR, since 2C hasn't closed. No gold label has been made, and the labelling page has saved nothing.

| `6cd57e2` | `POLICY.md`, before any draw or label (RDR-3) |
| `aab6290` | your 400-word check, as a committed script |
| `2467e28` | decision 36's note on your calls: the reader on every candidate, and the 400-word check |
| `1c8d670` | the leakage check's runs: every five-word run of the whole text |
| `ba85e04` | the inclusive grouping, and `check_leakage.py` with its threshold justified |
| `06fe6cb` | the labelling page and its test |
| `{DRAW}` | the draw: `split.json` and `HASH`, with `check_leakage.py` passing |
| `{D37}` | decision 37, and the plan and RESUME notes |

## The gate

- **Tests and lint:** `make test` gives {TESTS} passed, and `make lint` exits 0.
- **Git order:** `POLICY.md` at `6cd57e2` comes before `split.json` and `HASH` at `{DRAW}`. The split records `POLICY.md`'s sha256.
- **The hash and the leakage check:** `HASH` holds `split.json`'s sha256, `2593375…836c7`. `check_leakage.py` exits 0 (`eval/results/phase2c/leakage.json`):
  - no group crosses the split
  - no pool article reprints a gold or dev one by whole text
  - no dev article reprints a gold one
  - none of `POLICY.md`'s 63 examples is drawn, sits in a drawn article's group, or is reprinted in gold or dev
- **The calls:** decision 36's note went in at `2467e28`, and decision 37 at `{D37}`.

## The draw (decision 37)

- **The split:** 300 gold and 150 dev articles, in 17 strata, seeded. Each article's `pi` and `weight` are in `split.json`.
  - The strata are three edge slices (E8, E6, E12) and the years before 1850.
  - Then come lexicon v2's five rules, rarest first, and v1's terms alone, each split by whether a ghost term is in the headline.
  - Last, 25 near misses, from the reservoir in proportion to each year's pool.
  - Within a stratum the draw is systematic in date order. Gold has 22 articles from before 1850.
- **Expected reports in gold: 35.3** at the judged rates. Adding each stratum's Wilson ends gives 14.0 to 86.5.
  - E6 holds no judged item and E8 just one, so the estimate counts none of their reports. Under `POLICY.md`, a phantom sighting (rule 14) and an exposed hoax (rule 7) are reports.
  - At 35 reports, a field that's right in 30 has a Wilson interval of 71–94%.
- **Dev:** 150 articles, with gold's design at half the size. They're drawn from outside gold's groups, and none had to be redrawn. I label dev by hand under `POLICY.md` in 2C.2, alongside gold, so model selection aims at gold's truth rather than the teacher's.
- **The grouping:** 108,967 groups of two or more, holding 474,805 of the frame's 1,546,385 articles. The largest holds 1,098.
- **The whole-text check** quarantined 1,196 pool articles outside their groups. They reprint 142 of the 450 gold and dev articles.
  - Most are short repeated texts: mediums' cards and patent-medicine adverts re-run in later issues, timetables, market columns and shared wire passages.
  - A short text has too few sampled runs for a link, which is why the grouping misses them.
- **The pool:** 1,539,818 articles, with 6,567 held out.

## For you

1. **About 35 reports, or more?** About 50 would take about 70 more articles in v1's headline stratum, taken from the near misses, the bulk and the early decades. I kept those strata: they measure triage, the bulk's kinds, and B8's early decades. If you want 50, I'll redraw before any label.
2. **Dev's labeller is me, by hand under `POLICY.md`, in 2C.2.** Say if you'd rather have the teacher label it.
3. **Three of `POLICY.md`'s examples are outside the frame.** They're lexicon v1's random samples from eval A's screen, so they have no group. The check compares all 63 by whole text instead, and none is reprinted in gold or dev.
4. **A spelling mismatch.** `POLICY.md` writes `place_type` with spaces (`inn or hotel`) and the schema writes it with underscores. The page shows the first and saves the second. I left `POLICY.md` unchanged, since the split records its hash.
5. **For 2D: short texts link poorly.** The grouping and the stories miss short repeated texts, whose sampled runs are too few. The whole-text check found 1,196 such pool articles here, though none of these texts is likely to be a report.

1	# Gold labelling policy (RDR-3)
2	
3	These are the rules the gold set and the dev set are labelled by. This file was written and committed before the draw and before any label (decision 37). Every check of the reader rests on it.
4	
5	Each rule names an example by article id, from items eval A and lexicon v2 judged (decisions 27, 30 and 31). The draw leaves out those articles and their groups. An example's label here is this policy's, which can differ from the earlier judgment: rule 2 changes one.
6	
7	## What is labelled
8	
9	One article as AmericanStories gives it: its headline, its OCR text, and the scan's crop where the OCR is unclear.
10	- Label what the article says, not what is likely true.
11	- Label before seeing any model's output.
12	- When a later decision changes a rule, the labels it touches are checked again, and the change is dated.
13	
14	## kind
15	
16	Each article gets exactly one kind:
17	
18	| kind | What it is |
19	|---|---|
20	| `report` | A ghost, haunting, apparition, or spirit manifestation or communication, told as something that happened or was claimed to. It is tied to a particular occasion, place or person. |
21	| `fiction` | Stories, serials, poems, jokes, allegories and parodies, whatever their subject and however often reprinted. |
22	| `idiom` | A figure of speech: "give up the ghost", "not the ghost of a chance", haunt as a place frequented, "the spectre of war", "the ghost of the tariff". |
23	| `religious` | The Holy Ghost, sermons, hymns, prayers, Sunday-school lessons, saints, the Ghost Dance. |
24	| `advert` | An advertisement or a paid notice: patent medicines, theatre and illusion shows, books, real estate, and mediums' and clairvoyants' cards. |
25	| `other` | Everything else: names and titles, social events, OCR accidents, and essays or news about ghosts or spiritualism in general that tell no particular claim. |
26	
27	## Rules for hard cases
28	
29	1. **A ghost explained is still a report.** If the text gives a cause, the outcome is `explained`.
30	   - 1854: a voice taken for Phie's ghost is a trapped man, reached with a rope (`21_1854-11-16_p1_sn83021169_00514152792_1854111601_0398.json`): report, explained.
31	2. **Delusions and hallucinations, one rule.** A person's claim to have seen, heard or felt a ghost or spirit, on a particular occasion, is a report.
32	   - That holds whatever a court, a doctor or the paper makes of the person's mind.
33	   - Where the text calls the claim a delusion, a hallucination or insanity, the outcome is `explained`.
34	   - 1904: a defendant in court points at a spectre the paper calls imaginary (`6_1904-05-28_p1_sn84020358_00271744432_1904052801_1153.json`): report, explained.
35	   - 1909: a lunacy hearing, with spooks among a man's claims of persecution (`24_1909-08-31_p1_sn83025121_00294552327_1909083101_0987.json`): report, explained. **This overrules eval A's `other`.**
36	   - With no ghost or spirit claimed, a delusion is `other`. 1917: an insane man believes he is an aeroplane (`32_1917-11-02_pna_sn84024827_00211104776_1917110201_0388.json`).
37	3. **Spirit control, and a felt presence of the dead.** It is a report when a dead person's spirit is claimed, on a particular occasion, to have:
38	   - controlled someone
39	   - spoken or written through them
40	   - been felt present
41	
42	   Examples:
43	   - 1895, Waterloo, Oregon: a man speaks under the control of Sitting Bull's spirit (`1_1895-05-24_pna_sn97071028_00416152664_1895052401_0955.json`).
44	   - 1898: a wife murderer's defence is that spirits controlled him (`8_1898-01-20_pNone_sn84029386_00295871477_1898012001_0669.json`).
45	   - 1918: a scout feels a touch on the shoulder with no one by, and takes it for the spirits of the unburied dead (`9_1918-04-21_p1_sn83030214_00206532257_1918042102_0461.json`).
46	   - A trance or hypnotism with no spirit claimed is `other`:
47	     - 1897, Alexandria: a trance prophecy (`16_1897-01-02_p7_sn84024442_211103073_1897010201_0249.json`)
48	     - 1902, Old Bridge: a hypnotized woman names a murderer (`21_1902-11-24_pna_sn84024441_100492052_1902112401_0152.json`)
49	     - 1888: Tennyson's waking trance (`40_1888-12-05_pna_sn90059522_00175033373_1888120501_0403.json`)
50	4. **Séance reports.** A séance told as having happened, with phenomena or messages claimed, is a report, whatever the writer thinks of them.
51	   - 1857, Middlebury: a spirit called Judd speaks through a trance medium (`17_1857-07-29_pna_sn83025667_00280777808_1857072901_0724.json`).
52	   - 1875, Chittenden: fourteen spirits materialize at the Eddys' (`4_1875-03-29_pna_sn84022473_00280777559_1875032901_0300.json`).
53	   - 1898, Sacramento: John Slater's test séance (`4_1898-01-12_pna_sn82015104_00280768790_1898011201_0105.json`).
54	   - A séance announced for later, or spiritualists in the news with no phenomenon told, is `other`.

56	     - A French *séance* that is only a sitting of a body is `other`: 1890 (`26_1890-03-08_p1_sn88064492_00295874727_1890030802_0087.json`).

58	   - 1922: Conan Doyle says he has many times spoken with his dead son at séances (`12_1922-04-14_p2_sn85042243_00212478854_1922041401_0708.json`).

69	     - 1883: a letter against spiritualism (`38_1883-02-15_pna_sn85025620_00212479330_1883021501_0023.json`)
70	     - 1863: an essay doubting ghosts (`25_1863-10-09_pna_sn84023127_00280777006_1863100901_0373.json`)
71	7. **Hoax exposures.**
72	   - A ghost or spirit claimed, and then exposed as a deliberate deception, is a report with the outcome `hoax`. That covers a fraudulent séance caught out, or a prankster in a sheet taken for a ghost and caught.
73	   - An exposure in general, with no particular claim exposed, isn't a report:
74	     - 1878: an advertised show by Irving Bishop exposing mediums' tricks (`8_1878-05-09_pna_sn85033139_00271769349_1878050901_0475.json`): `advert`
